title: Network traffic prediction model based on WT-TBiLSTM
From Entanglement to Explanation: Bridging Quantum ML and XAI for Network Traffic Classification
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) promises computational advantages over Deep Learning (DL), but its effectiveness in practical network Traffic Classification (TC) remains underexplored. In this paper, we provide the first systematic use of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to interpret QMLbased classifiers for (mobile) network TC. We combine (a) SHAPbased attribution and (b) calibration analysis to compare QML and DL models across both small- and large-scale TC tasks. This dual perspective enables a deeper understanding of QML interpretability and reliability relative to DL in network TC, exposing key limitations and avenues for improvement.

title: Enhanced Intrusion Detection Using PSO Feature Selection with LSTM Gated RNN Based on Inactive Packet Bit Classification in Active Routing Wireless Transmission
venue: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering
abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are essential for safeguarding wireless networks, particularly with the increasing frequency of sophisticated cyber threats. Traditional IDS approaches face challenges with high false positive rates and the complexity of identifying intrusions in dynamic network environments. This research introduces a novel IDS framework that combines particle swarm optimization (PSO) for optimal feature selection with a gated long short-term memory (LSTM) network for accurate intrusion classification. PSO reduces feature dimensionality, enhancing computational efficiency by selecting only the most relevant attributes from network traffic data. The gated LSTM network is applied to capture temporal dependencies, allowing for precise classification of active and inactive packet bits to detect real-time anomalies. This combined PSO-LSTM approach effectively minimizes false positives, reduces computational complexity, and ensures robust intrusion detection, proving highly efficient for security in active wireless network environments. This framework’s enhanced detection rates and reduced time complexity highlight its potential to set a new benchmark in IDS performance for wireless networks. The performance metrics, such as precision, accuracy, recall, and F1-score, improve intrusion detection based on inactive packet bit classification in active routing wireless transmission. Experimental results evaluated with the KDDcup99 dataset show that our proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 93.61%, with a precision rate of 94.26%, a recall rate of 94.01%, and F1-score of 94.03%, outperforming the conventional deep learning methods such as deep neural networks (DNNs) and fuzzy neural networks (FNNs).

title: Combining Side-Channel Features with Deep Learning for Network Traffic Anomaly Detection
venue: Conference proceedings/Conference proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
abstract: As cybersecurity threats evolve, detecting anomalous network traffic is crucial for protecting information systems. However, this field still faces challenges such as data imbalance, feature extraction difficulties, and inadequate model performance. To address these challenges, this paper designs an anomaly detection model based on side-channel feature selection and random forest dimensionality reduction. Specifically, side-channel feature extraction explores potential features in network traffic data, capturing implicit information often missed by traditional methods. Subsequently, random forest importance scoring is used for feature selection and optimization. Additionally, the model also integrates the attention mechanism and bidirectional long short-term memory network. In experiments, the proposed method demonstrates outstanding performance in the CIC-IDS2017 and CIC UNSW-NB15 datasets, achieving accuracies of 98.90% and 98.67%, respectively, providing an effective strategy to strengthen network security defenses.

title: Scalable AI-Driven Framework for Detecting and Classifying Network Attacks
abstract: Since traditional heuristic-based detection systems mostly rely on predefined signatures and fixed patterns, cybersecurity has become a key concern due to the growing sophistication of cyber attacks. In order to get around these restrictions, this study suggests an AI-powered intrusion classification framework that can identify and categorize different kinds of attacks. Each of these attack types represents a different threat level, necessitating sophisticated detection techniques. The framework makes use of supervised techniques that are well-known for their high accuracy and versatility with regard to complicated datasets. The implementation phase will involve model validation using commonly used benchmark datasets, which cover a wide range of contemporary cyber-attack vectors, even if the current work is only at the framework design stage. The suggested solution is appropriate for real-time deployment in dynamic contexts because it was created with modularity and scalability in mind. A fundamental framework for creating intelligent security systems that can proactively identify complex threats, reduce false alarms, and greatly improve the overall resilience of network infrastructures is presented in this paper.

title: Hybrid Best Feature Selection using Deep Learning Techniques for Scalable Cyber Threat Detection
abstract: The growing complexity and scale of cybersecurity threats highlight the urgent need for advanced Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). In counter to these confrontation, this experiment producess a new hybrid framework called Hybrid Best Feature Selection with Deep Learning (HBFS-DL), which aims to improve cyber threat prediction. The HBFS-DL framework integrates effective feature engineering methods with DL techniques to remove redundant features and retain the most valuable ones, thereby boosting classification accuracy. The approach was tested on widely used datasets, CICIDS2017 and CSECICIDS2018, achieving notable accuracy rates of 96.4% and 98.5% subsequently.These facts authenticate the efficiency rate of the proposed framework in responding to the advancing needs of cybersecurity.

title: Comprehensive Analysis on Machine learning and Deep learning based Intrusion Detection in the Internet of Things
venue: International Conference on Mobile Networks and Wireless Communications (ICMNWC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a growing technology in recent years, which requires a secure and efficient technique to protect IoT networks. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) offer an essential support to the protection of these networks against harmful threats. The Machine learning (ML) and Deep learning (DL) techniques can self-learn, dynamically detect threats, and efficiently adapt. Hence, ML and DL techniques help in minimizing false positives and effectively respond to new vulnerabilities. This survey gives an exhaustive review of existing methods and models of intrusion detection in the environments of IoT. It analyses data extraction methods, loss functions, evaluation measures, and the most commonly referred algorithms. This study provides different research papers to group based on ML and DL techniques. The survey also summarises the well-known dataset named IoT intrusion detection datasets, which has both advantages, drawbacks, outlining characteristics, and computational efficiency to measure the feasibility of practical use of IDS models. The survey recommends lightweight and resource-efficient IDS to support resource-limited IoT devices and uses high-quality representative data for new developments in IoT security

title: Enhanced FNN Architecture for Intrusion Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks: Optimized Detection Efficiency
venue: International Conference on Mobile Networks and Wireless Communications (ICMNWC)
abstract: To achieve high detection accuracy and reduce false alarms in a heterogeneous network setup, this paper suggests a strong Wireless Sensor Network Intrusion Detection System (WSN-IDS) which is a Feedforward Neural Network (FNN) with a dense 256-layer system. The model is trained and tested on three benchmark datasets that include CCID 2017, WSN-DS, WSN-BFSF and include many different intrusion scenarios including DDoS, Blackhole, Flooding, Grayhole, Forwarding and TDMA attacks. The results of the proposed FNN-Dense 256 architecture show that it has very good detection accuracy of 0.9996 with AUC values of 1.0 on both normal and DDoS classes on the CCID 2017 dataset. It achieves a record of 0.9885 to 0.999 on the WSN-DS dataset and between 0.9688 and 0.9947 on the WSN-BFSF dataset with AUC value ranging between 0.98 to 1.0. The system has a False Positive Rate (FPR) of less than 0.001 in most of the attacks indicating the high reliability and strength of the system. These results validate the claim that the FNN-Dense 256 model is an effective generalization and adaptability in detection of various intrusions in IoT-driven WSNs, and thus, a good solution to real-time, lightweight, and energy-saving intrusion detection systems.

title: Instantaneous Detection of Anomalous Behavior in IoT Systems via Responsive Learning Algorithms
abstract: Security in the Internet of Things (IoT) is a sub-domain of cybersecurity that prevents various files, data, devices, and networks from malicious attacks. In this paper, a rapid system for detecting abnormal behavior in IoT systems using fusion-based learning algorithms (FBLA) is presented. The proposed FBLA is integrated with an ensemble deep learning (DL) model to learn the malicious behaviour patterns online. The FBLA is a combination of a Transformer with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), along with an Isolation Forest, to develop a lightweight anomaly detection mechanism. The proposed FBLA prevents anomalies based on abnormal behavior. The training model RTIDS (Robust Transformer-based Intrusion Detection System) is used to identify the behavior of attackers and transfer these behavioral patterns to FBLA for effective classification of attacks. The benchmark datasets were applied to IoT datasets to analyze the performance of FBLA and other existing models. The proposed FBLA achieved a high performance in terms of malicious detection rate.

title: CAT-Mamba: A State Space Model Approach for Encrypted Malicious Traffic Detection
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace
abstract: As a key enabler of energy transformation, the new-type power system is increasingly exposed to sophisticated cybersecurity threats due to its rapid digitalization and interconnection. Although sequence models have become the dominant solution in network traffic detection owing to their strength in modeling long-range dependencies, their limited sensitivity to local patterns and susceptibility to data imbalance constrain further improvements in detection accuracy. To address these issues, we propose CAT-Mamba, a novel detection framework for encrypted malicious traffic that integrates multi-scale convolutional processing and state space modeling. Specifically, a multi-scale feature fusion module is introduced to capture spatial and local traffic features, thereby enhancing the representation of fine-grained patterns. Subsequently, a Mamba is used to model the temporal dynamics of traffic sequences. To further mitigate the spatial and perceptual limitations of the state space model, channel and spatial attention mechanisms are incorporated as gating functions, boosting both global and local feature modeling. Additionally, a Class-Aware attention block is designed to enhance the recognition of minority class samples. Experimental results demonstrate that CAT-Mamba achieves F1-scores of 98.01% and 100% on the CICIDS-2017 and UNSW-NB15 datasets, respectively, and 99.98% on the UNSW-MG24 dataset tailored for microgrid scenarios, validating the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method in complex network traffic environments.

title: Feature Space Compression for Intrusion Classification: Comparative Insights from a Linear Unsupervised Perspective
abstract: The proliferation and prevalence of cutting-edge information technologies have contributed the most to the generation of high-volume data. Working in tandem with such voluminous data often makes the identification of network infiltration more tedious and time-consuming. Fortunately, advanced machine learning techniques have the potential to cope with the high dimensionality (volume) of data. Nevertheless, the appropriateness of dimension reduction techniques remains a matter of concern when processing time, effort, and the extraction of valuable information are key considerations, especially in the context of intrusion detection. In light of existing techniques, this paper experiments and assesses the classification performance of prevalent dimensionality reduction approaches like Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Independent Component Analysis (ICA), Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Random Projection (RP) and Factor Analysis (FA) on CICIDS2017 dataset along with different dimensions on K-nearest neighbor classifier. The study provides practical guidance for selecting an effective reduction strategy for intrusion detection by comparing key evaluation metrics, including mean squared error (MSE).

title: Intrusion Detection for Internet of Vehicles Based on Deep and Machine Learning with XAI Interpretation
abstract: This research develops an Intrusion Detection for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) by testing four different algorithms: two Machine Learning models (XGBoost and Random Forest) and two Deep Learning models, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). Since vehicles today are connected and exchange a lot of data, protecting this data from attacks is very important. The study focuses not only on how well the models can detect attacks but also on explaining how they make decisions using Explainable AI (XAI) methods called Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME). This helps increase trust in the system by showing which parts of the vehicle network data led to an attack alert. The results show that XGBoost and Random Forest perform very well, reaching about 99% accuracy while maintaining a false alarm rate under 1 %, demonstrating strong reliability for IoV intrusion detection. The LSTM and TCN models also do a good job with accuracy above 95 %, especially in understanding the time-based patterns in the data. The urgency of this research comes from the growing threats to connected vehicles which can lead to serious safety issues, and real-world vehicle network traffic data. Therefore, it is crucial to have an Intrusion Detection that not only finds attacks accurately but is also easy to understand and trust, making this work important for improving security in future smart vehicles and transportation systems.

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model Based on Spatio-Temporal Feature Mining for Traffic Analysis in Industrial Internet Gateway
abstract: As the scale of the Industrial Internet continues to expand, the number of network connections and data traffic are experiencing explosive growth. Security threats and attack types targeting the Industrial Internet are becoming increasingly complex, rendering traditional firewalls and encryption/decryption technologies inadequate for addressing diverse and sophisticated attack scenarios. Furthermore, traffic characteristics within the Industrial Internet environment exhibit significant asymmetry, such as a highly imbalanced distribution between benign and malicious traffic. To address this challenge, this paper proposes CBiNet—a hybrid deep learning model that integrates a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) with a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM). Designed to effectively learn and leverage such asymmetric spatio-temporal patterns, experimental validation demonstrates that the CBiNet model can efficiently tackle complex traffic identification tasks in industrial internet environments. It provides a highly accurate, scalable intrusion detection method for securing industrial internet gateways.

title: SERA: Semantic Entity Recognition and Alignment for Threat Intelligence Representation
venue: IEEE International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
abstract: With the increasing sophistication of cyber attacks, traditional defense mechanisms have become inadequate due to information asymmetry between attackers and defenders. While threat intelligence sharing helps bridge this gap, existing entity recognition methods face two critical challenges: (1) difficulty in handling domain-specific features and entity ambiguity in cybersecurity texts; and (2) ineffective alignment of heterogeneous entities across multi-source threat intelligence. To address these issues, we propose the Semantic Entity Recognition and Alignment (SERA) framework, which employs SecureBERT to construct security-domain semantic representations and learn specialized threat intelligence features. The framework combines bidirectional long short-Term memory (BiLSTM) to capture contextual dependencies, incorporates an attention mechanism to enhance key semantic modeling, and finally utilizes a Conditional Random Field (CRF) layer to improve label sequence consistency. To resolve entity naming inconsistencies and representation redundancy, we integrate three types of information—semantic similarity, structural embedding similarity, and contextual similarity—and perform multi-source entity alignment through weighted scoring, effectively improving cross-source entity unification. Experimental results on the DNRTI dataset demonstrate that the SERA model achieves superior performance compared to baseline models, with an F1-score of 0.7821, precision of 0.7625, recall of 0.8152, and entity recognition accuracy of 0.9387.

title: A novel intrusion detection system for class imbalance datasets using hybrid sampling with deep learning techniques
Feature importance guided autoencoder for dimensionality reduction in intrusion detection systems
abstract: Intrusion detection systems (IDS) play a vital role in protecting computer networks from malicious activities. Dimensionality reduction techniques are commonly employed to enhance the effectiveness and accuracy of machine learning based IDS. In this study, we proposed an effective dimensionality reduction technique called feature importance-based autoencoder (FI-AE) for intrusion detection systems. Our proposed approach encompasses several key components. First, we introduce a novel feature importance method known as one-versus-all feature importance (OVA), which utilizes a random forest algorithm. Next, we train an autoencoder model using a weighted loss function that takes into account the feature importance values obtained through the OVA method. Finally, we utilized the trained autoencoder to reduce the number of features in the benchmark datasets, followed by the application of a random forest classifier to the reduced datasets. We tested our proposed model using three well-known datasets, namely NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CIC-IDS2017. The experiments revealed that the random forest classifier, combined with our proposed model, outperformed previous dimensionality reduction techniques in terms of accuracy and F1-score.

title: Supervised and deep learning techniques for DDoS detection in software-defined network architectures: a systematic review
venue: Engineering Science and Technology an International Journal
abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers significant advantages over traditional network architectures by providing flexibility, programmability and centralized control in network management. However, the centralized nature of this architecture brings new vulnerabilities, especially against security threats such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. In this context, Machine Learning (ML) based methods offer effective and innovative solutions for detecting DDoS attacks in SDN environments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of machine learning techniques for DDoS attack detection in SDN-based networks. The most remarkable aspect is that, unlike many existing works in the literature, it does not only focus on general detection methods, but also examines in detail various scenarios in different application areas of SDN, such as Internet of Things (IoT), SCADA systems, 5G and mobile networks, and vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANET). This provides a holistic perspective on the security dynamics of SDN architecture in different contexts and comparatively evaluates current threats and solution approaches in these areas. In the study, the success, usage areas and limitations of different machine learning algorithms (supervised, unsupervised and deep learning methods) in detecting DDoS attacks are analyzed and conclusions are made to guide researchers. In this respect, the study contributes to the literature on SDN security in terms of both technical depth and application diversity.

title: A deep residual 1D-CNN with self-attention for fraud transaction detection in virtual economies
abstract: As virtual economies in the metaverse continue to grow, the need for real-time risk assessment in financial transactions has become critical. Traditional fraud detection systems often face challenges in keeping pace with the complexity and speed of metaverse data. To address this, we introduce a real-time anomaly detection and risk classification model designed specifically for metaverse transactions. The model is based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) enhanced with residual connections and a self-attention mechanism, allowing it to focus on the most relevant features of each transaction for improved risk classification. We trained the model on benchmark metaverse financial datasets from Kaggle, achieving excellent results in accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity when classifying transactions into three risk levels-low, moderate, and high. To validate its robustness, we also tested it on the widely used Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset, where it maintained strong performance. However, we acknowledge that perfect scores can sometimes indicate overly clean or predictable data. To address this, we conducted an ablation study by introducing controlled noise into the dataset, evaluating the model's ability to handle uncertainty and imperfections in real-world scenarios. To enhance interpretability, we analyzed feature importance across several CNN-based variations and assessed performance using confusion matrices, ROC curves, and t-SNE visualizations, which confirmed clear separation of risk levels in high-dimensional space. Further comparisons with other machine learning and deep learning models demonstrate the confidence and effectiveness of the proposed 1D-CNN architecture for financial fraud detection in the metaverse.

title: A survey on recent recurrent neural networks based intrusion detection systems
A hybrid MaOEA-ML framework for network intrusion detection system in the Internet of Health Things (IoHT)
Enhancing Threat Hunting in Wazuh through a Hybrid Random Forest Model: A Comparative Study for Reducing MTTD and MTTR in Cybersecurity Operations
abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyberattacks demands intelligent, adaptive Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) capable of rapid threat detection and response. This study proposes a Hybrid Random Forest (HRF) model integrated with the Wazuh platform to enhance threat hunting by reducing Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Respond (MTTR). The model is evaluated on two benchmark datasets, CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and ToN_IoT, using a methodology aligned with state-of-the-art approaches, including data preprocessing, Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC)-based feature selection, and Min-Max normalization. The results show high detection accuracies of 99.12% and 99.65% on the respective datasets, with significantly lower inference time compared to deep learning models. Integration with Wazuh enables real-time alerting and automated response, reducing MTTD and MTTR by up to 75% and 65%. A comparative analysis against a hybrid GRU-BiLSTM baseline reveals that while the HRF model achieves slightly lower accuracy on ToN_IoT, it outperforms it on CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and offers superior computational efficiency. This work presents a practical framework for deploying lightweight machine learning models in operational environments, demonstrating that ensemble methods like Random Forest are viable, interpretable, and operationally efficient alternatives to deep learning for proactive cybersecurity operations.

title: Wireless Sensor Networks Security Using SACCGAN‐RSA in a Novel Deep Learning–Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Enhancing
abstract: ABSTRACT Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are essential to cyber–physical systems with their multiple hop, self‐organized arrangement of mobile sensor components. WSNs sense, aggregate, process, and transfer data across a geographical network area, ultimately forwarding it to the network's head. Nevertheless, existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) for WSNs face various limitations such as less detection rates, high computational costs, and significant false alarm rates due to resource constraints, redundancy, and data correlation. To address these challenges, a self‐attention–based cycle‐consistent generative adversarial network (SACCGAN), enhanced using reptile search algorithm for intrusion detection in WSN environments (SACCGAN‐RSA‐IDS‐WSN), is proposed. The data are collected through WSN‐DS dataset and supplied to the preprocessing stage. Preprocessing involves adjusted quick shift phase preserving dynamic range compression (AQS‐PDC) to address missing values and remove redundant data. The feature selection is done by Pelican optimization algorithm (POA) to identify ideal features. Utilizing the selected features, SACCGAN categorizes WSN data into normal and anomalous instances, including blackhole, grayhole, flooding, and scheduling attacks. However, SACCGAN lacks adaptation of optimization modes to ensure accurate WSN intrusion detection. Therefore, the reptile search algorithm (RSA) is introduced to enhance SACCGAN parameters effectively. The proposed SACCGAN‐RSA‐IDS‐WSN is executed in Python using WSN‐DS database. The SACCGAN‐RSA‐IDS‐WSN approach is examined under some metrics like recall, precision, F‐measure, specificity, accuracy, RoC, and computation time. The SACCGAN‐RSA‐IDS‐WSN method attains 28.59%, 31.43%, and 30.18% higher accuracy; 33.45%, 37.67%, and 27.78% higher ROC; 31.73%, 33.49%, and 29.15% lower computational time when compared with existing techniques.

title: Diffusion Multimodal Distillation Collaboration: A Generative Equilibrium Framework for Efficient Vehicle Networking Intrusion Detection
abstract: Real-time intrusion detection with millisecond response is critical for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) security but is challenged by extreme class imbalance and high computational costs. This paper proposes a novel multimodal framework integrating Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) and Knowledge Distillation (KD). First, multi-source data is transformed into RGB images. A conditional DDPM with timestep and class embeddings balances datasets by generating minority-class samples. The teacher model (DiffuGuardian) fuses text-image features for training. Subsequently, a lightweight student model, LiteSentinel, is designed employing depthwise separable convolutions and inverted residual blocks to reduce parameters. Results on three datasets demonstrate that DiffuGuardian consistently achieves around 98–100% precision, accuracy, recall, and F1-score under 5-fold evaluation, while LiteSentinel maintains approximately 95–99% across all metrics with substantially reduced complexity. DiffuGuardian reaches an inference time of 3.80ms with a model size of 0.10 MB, whereas LiteSentinel further reduces latency to 0.79ms with a size of 0.07 MB, enabling efficient edge deployment for IoV security.

title: AI-Powered Predictive Ransomware and Malware Detection for Edge and Cloud Systems
abstract: The rapid growth of edge and cloud infrastructures has increased the attack surface for ransomware and advanced malware. As a result, there is an urgent need to improve predictive defenses. This work introduces an AI-driven ransomware and malware detection system, leveraging Federated Deep Learning (FDL), behavior-based analytics, and graph reasoning to identify and stop ransomware and malware before they cause any damage. Unlike traditional signature or anomaly-based systems, the proposed framework focuses on learning in both temporal and spatial domains. This is achieved by utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to model the relationships between system entities and Transformer encoders to capture the changes of these relations over time. It makes accurate predictions of zero-day threats by fusing data from system call graphs, encrypted and non-encrypted network traffic, and process lineage information in a multi-layer threat intelligence fusion engine. The model is trained in a privacy-preserving and scalable way using energy-efficient federated learning, thus enabling edge devices to contribute to global defense strategies without revealing raw data. The system performs with 98.7% detection accuracy, reduces detection latency by 46%, and decreases false alarm rates by 62%, when compared to the state-of-the-art systems, according to the tests on hybrid real-world datasets. This work provides a basis for autonomous, explainable, and adaptive cybersecurity in the environment of edge-cloud, heading toward predictive cyber resilience in Intelligent Distributed Systems.

title: An integrated multi-criteria decision-making framework for assessing and ranking intrusion detection systems
abstract: Abstract Intrusion Detection Systems are critical for safeguarding networked environments against evolving cyber threats. Machine Learning offers a variety of ID models; however, assessing their performance to select the one that best fit Decision-Makers needs is particularly challenging since it involves balancing conflicting performance criteria. This paper proposes an integrated framework that combines multiple Multi-Criteria Decision-Making approaches to identify the most effective ID model across diverse operational contexts acknowledging that a single method may not yield a robust and trusted assessment. In this framework, thirty-one ID models based on representative ML algorithms (e.g., DT, NN, etc) are benchmarked on three widely used ID datasets, NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CIC-IDS2018, using nine performance criteria (e.g., accuracy, recall, etc). To capture differing priorities across criteria, objective weights for the criteria are derived via four distinct methods (CILOS, Shannon Entropy, CRITIC, and MEREC). Afterwards, ten distinct ranking algorithms (e.g., TOPSIS, GRA, etc) are applied with each weighting scheme; this yields 120 individual rank-orders which are then synthesized through Majority voting, Borda count and Copeland integration methods into a final, consensus ranking, thus boosting result stability and enhancing stakeholders’ confidence. In addition, a sensitivity analysis is carried out at different levels, including weighting methods, ranking methods, dataset level and criteria level to evaluate the robustness of the framework. The results consistently highlight the 1D-CNN architecture as the top performer, while also revealing complementary specialist and all-rounder models under different aggregation schemes. By integrating extensive algorithmic diversity with principled weight computation, a robust, low-bias mechanism for ID model selection is delivered by the framework, which can be adapted by practitioners to shifting threat landscapes and evaluation priorities.

title: Cyberattack detection using a golden pelican search algorithm optimized three-tier deep learning approach
A one-dimensional convolutional neural network framework for photovoltaic array fault detection
abstract: Abstract Faults in the photovoltaic (PV) array radically disrupt power production, system operation, and efficiency. Detecting the PV array faults becomes a challenging task as fault characteristics and normal operating conditions exhibit the same characteristics under certain conditions. This paper introduces an innovative framework for fault detection in PV arrays using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). Initially, the fault signatures of hot spot faults, line-ground faults, and short circuit faults in the 3.2 kW PV array are dissected to determine the appropriate measurements for fault detection and discrimination. It is found that the PV array measurements, such as voltage, current, power, and their derivatives, provide distinct fault characteristics, and it would be helpful to discriminate between the faults. The datasets used for training and testing are generated with the selected measurements under different operating conditions. The effectiveness of the proposed 1D-CNN-based PV array fault detection (1D-CNN-PVFD) framework is appraised using confusion matrix analysis and contrasted with the recently presented machine learning techniques found in the literature, namely kNN, SVM, and ANN. The 1D-CNN-PVFD framework outperforms the different techniques with an accuracy of 99.44% and demonstrates promising consistency in performance.

title: Denoising Adaptive Multi-Branch Architecture for Detecting Cyber Attacks in Industrial Internet of Services
abstract: The emerging scope of the Industrial Internet of Services (IIoS) requires a robust intrusion detection system to detect malicious attacks. The increasing frequency of sophisticated and high-impact cyber attacks has resulted in financial losses and catastrophes in IIoS-based manufacturing industries. However, existing solutions often struggle to adapt and generalize to new cyber attacks. This study proposes a unique approach designed for known and zero-day network attack detection in IIoS environments, called Denoising Adaptive Multi-Branch Architecture (DA-MBA). The proposed approach is a smart, conformal, and self-adjusting cyber attack detection framework featuring denoising representation learning, hybrid neural inference, and open-set uncertainty calibration. The model merges a denoising autoencoder (DAE) to generate noise-tolerant latent representations, which are processed using a hybrid multi-branch classifier combining dense and bidirectional recurrent layers to capture both static and temporal attack signatures. Moreover, it addresses challenges such as adaptability and generalizability by hybridizing a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM). The proposed hybrid model was designed to fuse feed-forward transformations with sequence-aware modeling, which can capture direct feature interactions and any underlying temporal and order-dependent patterns. Multiple approaches have been applied to strengthen the dual-branch architecture, such as class weighting and comprehensive hyperparameter optimization via Optuna, which collectively address imbalanced data, overfitting, and dynamically shifting threat vectors. The proposed DA-MBA is evaluated on two widely recognized IIoT-based datasets, Edge-IIoT set and WUSTL-IIoT-2021 and achieves over 99% accuracy and a near 0.02 loss, underscoring its effectiveness in detecting the most sophisticated attacks and outperforming recent deep learning IDS baselines. The solution offers a scalable and flexible architecture for enhancing cybersecurity within evolving IIoS environments by coupling feature denoising, multi-branch classification, and automated hyperparameter tuning. The results confirm that coupling robust feature denoising with sequence-aware classification can provide a scalable and flexible framework for improving cybersecurity within the IIoS. The proposed architecture offers a scalable, interpretable, and risk sensitive defense mechanism for IIoS, advancing secure, adaptive, and trustworthy industrial cyber-resilience.

title: Multi-feature unsupervised time series anomaly detection based on memory-augmented autoencoder - One-Class support vector machine
Forest Fire Prediction using One Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
abstract: Forest fires have caused a critical threat, leading to severe environmental degradation, economic losses and serious consequences for human life. Prediction, prevention, and control to handle forest fires become important. Several studies have applied machine learning for forest fire prediction. In this study, one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN) was implemented to forest fire prediction using the UCI Algerian forest fire dataset. This dataset contains 12 features and 244 instances. The proposed model was measured using standard metrics—accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score—and its performance is compared with baseline algorithms including SVM, Random Forest and XG-Boost. Based this experiment, 1D CNN achieves higher performance than existing traditional models, although its performance remains slightly below that of optimized model in previous studies. These findings indicate that 1D CNN offers a competitive deep-learning method for forest fire prediction and provides a useful benchmark for future research.

title: A Semantic-Aware Network Intelligence Framework for Anomaly Detection using Large Language Models
venue: IEEE International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
abstract: As enterprise networks grow in complexity, detecting sophisticated and covert anomalous traffic has become a critical challenge. This paper presents SENTINEL, a framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) into anomaly detection by converting traffic logs into natural language and generating semantic embeddings. These embeddings are fused with traditional numerical features to form enriched representations, processed through a Denoising Autoencoder and a Transformer to capture temporal patterns. Experiments on a large enterprise dataset (ZE-CDT) show that SENTINEL achieves notable performance, with ablation studies confirming the clear benefits of LLM-based semantic augmentation for more context-aware intrusion detection.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Proactive and Interpretable Intrusion Detection
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks (CICN)
abstract: The growing sophistication of cyberattacks necessitates intelligent intrusion detection systems (IDS) that can not only classify malicious traffic but also forecast attack trends. In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates dense feed-forward layers with sequential encoders (Bi-LSTM and Transformer) for intrusion classification, while employing a GRU-based forecasting module to capture temporal attack dynamics. The CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset was utilized, incorporating 78 network traffic features across multiple attack types. To ensure interpretability, SHAP-based explanations were applied, enabling identification of key features such as Destination Port and Flow Duration that influenced model decisions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 97.8 %, an F1-score of 0.972, and an AUC of 0.985, with a low false alarm rate of 2.1 %. Forecasting experiments further achieved an RMSE of 14.6 and a MAPE of 3.8 %, validating the effectiveness of the time-series module in providing proactive alerts. Compared with machine learning and deep learning baselines, the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing methods, offering a reliable, accurate, and interpretable IDS for next-generation cybersecurity applications.

title: Optimizing Deep Q-Networks for Intrusion Detection: A Mixed-Variable PSO with Dual Encoding
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Communication Networks (CICN)
abstract: Intrusion detection is a critical component of network security, yet traditional methods often struggle to cope with evolving threats. Deep Q-Learning (DQL), a form of deep reinforcement learning, offers adaptive and intelligent solutions to complex network environments. However, DQL's performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameters—both continuous and discrete—necessitating an effective optimization strategy. This study introduces DES-PSO (Dual-Encoding Scheme assisted Particle Swarm Optimization) within a mixed-variable framework to optimize the DQL model. The DE-PSO approach leverages binary and Gray encoding to efficiently handle heterogeneous hyperparameters, thereby enhancing search effectiveness and improving classification accuracy in intrusion detection tasks. Data augmentation techniques are further applied to strengthen system robustness. The framework is evaluated on the UNSW-NB15 dataset for binary classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high classification accuracy and robustness, offering a highly adaptable and effective solution for improving intrusion detection in complex network security environments.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Network Slicing for 5G: Enhancing QoS Management through Predictive Modeling
abstract: This chapter investigates the pivotal role of Network Slicing (NS) in optimizing the performance of Fifth-Generation (5G) mobile networks, which offer unprecedented connectivity through vast bandwidth, ultra-low latency, and scalability to support diverse Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. NS allows the segmentation of a physical network into multiple logical networks, each tailored to specific application needs, from mission-critical industrial automation to high-bandwidth video streaming. To classify user requests into the most appropriate Network Slices (NSs), the study applies Machine Learning (ML) models trained on an extensive 5G traffic dataset. Utilizing classical ML methods and advanced ensemble techniques, such as Support Vector Classifier (SVC), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), XGBoost, and Random Forest, the models achieve an impressive accuracy of 98.51%, outperforming previous benchmarks. The research contributes to the field through meticulous data preprocessing, including feature selection and oversampling to address class imbalance, as well as rigorous feature engineering to enhance model interpretability and efficiency. Cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization further ensure model robustness. The results highlight the critical role of ML-driven predictive modeling in improving NS deployment, resource allocation, and QoS management in 5G networks, thus enabling more efficient service delivery and a superior user experience.

title: A novel hybrid ensemble deep learning approach for cyber intrusion detection
abstract: The uninterrupted growth of transactions carried out over the Internet (e.g., adoption of digital payments) can lead to potential exposure to serious security problems. Regarding the implementation of innovative technological solutions, the scientific community strives to develop approaches which can effectively protect the entities from adversarial cyber-threats. This research focuses on improving network security, developing the Hybrid Ensemble Deep Learning Intrusion Detection System ( HEDL ∞ ). It is the optimized version of the previous two older releases, namely HEDL-IDS and HEDL - IDS 2 . The Ensemble consists of two Deep Neural Networks (DNN), four Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and five Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) with parallel LSTM layers. The classifier of each Ensemble employs an improved Custom Vote process, following the Weighted Vote and the Majority Vote principles. The HEDL ∞ was successfully validated on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, with overall accuracy equal to 99.56% during the training phase and 99.24% during the testing phase. The high values of the performance indices during testing confirm that the updated version is a robust tool that can be used in real-world, to significantly reduce the exposure of the network’s users, paving the way for further research efforts.

title: Toward Sustainable and Resilient Smart Cities Enhancing Downlink Scheduling and Cybersecurity in Saudi Arabia’s IoT Networks
Optimized AI-driven Malware detection and network attack identification using a lightweight gradient ensemble in IoT edge
Smart Intrusion Identification System with Machine Learning-Based Data-Driven Methods for Secure Cloud Infrastructure
abstract: IDS, which can identify many forms of network attacks, has been the subject of a thorough review of mountain of literature on subject. Cloud computing simplifies the process of utilizing resources on a demand-by-demand basis; however also exposes users to sophisticated hacking exploits. In such ever-changing settings, traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) often miss new threats. The paper introduces a Smart Intrusion Detection System based on ANN that effectively classifies normal and malicious traffic in networks as evidenced by using the NSL-KDD benchmark. Evaluation and training with standardized performance measures demonstrate that the model exceeds baseline models in relation to accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The experimental results show that the ANN model detects common and uncommon types of attacks with the minimum number of false positives and negatives, which indicates its accuracy as 97.5 percent. Comparatively, baseline models, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), registered lower performances. The findings show that the suggested ANN-based strategy for intelligent intrusion detection in current cloud computing systems is effective, reliable, and can be used in real-time.

title: A Novel CNN-BiLSTM Model with MultiHead Attention for Efficient Intrusion Detection
abstract: This study explores enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) through Deep Learning (DL) techniques, particularly CNN-BiLSTM architectures. Traditional IDS techniques struggle to detect evolving threats due to the rapid increase in cyber threats, including advanced attacks targeting network infrastructures. This work examines hybrid models, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for feature extraction and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks for analyzing temporal relationships in network traffic. Two benchmark datasets, NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15, train the models, achieving impressive accuracy rates of over 98.96% and 99.99% in binary classification tasks. The paper addresses high false alerts, anomaly detection, and the model's adaptability to various network environments. The results show that the proposed DL-based IDS models provide a solid foundation for accurate, scalable, and reliable intrusion detection, effectively identifying both normal and malicious traffic.

title: A Hybrid Autoencoder and Random Forest for Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: Malicious network activities are a significant cybersecurity challenge because of changing adversarial behaviours. This study introduces a stacked autoencoder-based intrusion detection framework that uses the UNSW-NB15 dataset. The framework condenses 45 network traffic features into a 32-dimensional coded vector. This process helps extract features. Categorical data is converted into a usable format. A standard scaler was applied to the features before training. The model combines deep learning's ability to identify patterns with Random Forest classification, achieving 93.51% accuracy, 96% precision, 92% recall, and 94% F1-score for attacks. This shows that stacked autoencoders and tree-based classifiers can effectively detect intrusions in complex network datasets.

title: HCA-IDS: A Semantics-Aware Heterogeneous Cross-Attention Network for Robust Intrusion Detection in CAVs
abstract: Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) are exposed to increasingly sophisticated cyber threats hidden within high-dimensional, heterogeneous network traffic. A critical bottleneck in existing Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) is the feature heterogeneity gap: discrete protocol signatures (e.g., flags, services) and continuous traffic statistics (e.g., flow duration, packet rates) reside in disjoint latent spaces. Traditional deep learning approaches typically rely on naive feature concatenation, which fails to capture the intricate, non-linear semantic dependencies between these modalities, leading to suboptimal performance on long-tail, minority attack classes. This paper proposes HCA-IDS, a novel framework centered on Semantics-Aware Cross-Modal Alignment. Unlike heavy-weight models, HCA-IDS adopts a streamlined Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) backbone optimized for edge deployment. We introduce a dedicated Multi-Head Cross-Attention mechanism that explicitly utilizes static “Pattern” features to dynamically query and re-weight relevant dynamic “State” behaviors. This architecture forces the model to learn a unified semantic manifold where protocol anomalies are automatically aligned with their corresponding statistical footprints. Empirical assessments on the NSL-KDD and CICIDS2018 datasets, validated through rigorous 5-Fold Cross-Validation, substantiate the robustness of this approach. The model achieves a Macro-F1 score of over 94% on 7 consolidated attack categories, exhibiting exceptional sensitivity to minority attacks (e.g., Web Attacks and Infiltration). Crucially, HCA-IDS is ultra-lightweight, with a model size of approximately 1.00 MB and an inference latency of 0.0037 ms per sample. These results confirm that explicit semantic alignment combined with a lightweight architecture is key to robust, real-time intrusion detection in resource-constrained CAVs.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Forecasting NIFTY50 and NIFTY500 Indices using Technical Indicators
abstract: The stock market forecasting is a challenging issue because of volatility, nonlinear, and dynamic nature. This paper explores the predictive capabilities of three deep learning algorithms: LSTM, GRU, and CNN-LSTM in predicting the weekly closing prices of the primary Indian stock indices such as NIFTY50 and NIFTY500. We developed a custom Weekly dataset having historical features such as Open, High, Low, Close and Volume (OHLCV) data and technical indicators. Technical indicators are derived using OHLCV data like Relative Strength Index (RSI), point difference, percentage difference are used. Evaluation of the models is performed on the basis of such metrics as the Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R2score. Findings indicate a superior performance of CNN-LSTM in predicting NIFTY50 and LSTM in predicting NIFTY500, which proves the usefulness of hybrid deep learning models in time series forecasting in the financial sector.

title: Advancements in AI-Based Botnet Detection Techniques for IoT Networks: A Comprehensive Survey

title: AI‐Powered Anomaly Detection for Secure Internet of Things (IoT): Optimising XGBoost and Deep Learning With Bayesian Optimisation
abstract: ABSTRACT Intelligent and adaptive defence systems that can quickly thwart changing cyberthreats are becoming more and more necessary in the dynamic and data‐intensive Internet of things (IoT) environment. Using the NSL‐KDD benchmark dataset, this paper presents an improved anomaly detection system that combines an optimised sequential neural network (OSNN) with an XGBoost model optimised using Bayesian approaches. Key drawbacks of conventional intrusion detection systems (IDSs), including manual hyperparameter tuning, extensive preprocessing and ineffective optimisation techniques, are successfully addressed by the suggested solution. By automating the adjustment of key parameters, such as learning rate, tree depth and regularisation strength, Bayesian optimisation enhances model convergence, prediction accuracy and generalisation. Superior binary classification performance was attained by the optimised XGBoost, which had 99.98% accuracy, 99.94% F1 score and 99.95% MCC. In a similar vein, the Bayesian‐optimised OSNN obtained flawless precision and recall for the normal and U2R classes, achieving 99.92% overall accuracy in multiclass identification. Across all attack types, its CNN‐based architecture showed excellent sensitivity and specificity, attaining almost flawless AUC values. The suggested Bayesian‐optimised framework offers a highly accurate, scalable and self‐adaptive intrusion detection solution for actual IoT network environments, outperforming traditional machine and deep learning models by a large margin overall.

title: Optimized intrusion detection using particle swarm optimization and neural networks in simulated and physical network environments
abstract: This method article presents a reproducible framework for constructing and evaluating an intrusion detection system using optimized machine learning workflows. Network traffic was collected by implementing two independently controlled setups: a software-based network model and a small-scale real hardware network, with packet traces recorded using Wireshark. These traces were merged with widely used reference datasets to ensure coverage of diverse attack behaviors. Feature dimensionality was reduced using Particle Swarm Optimization, enabling efficient learning while limiting redundant network attributes. The refined feature sets were subsequently used to train multiple classification models, including tree-based, distance-based, and neural learning approaches. Experimental evaluation shows that the neural model trained on PSO-selected features delivers the most stable detection behavior, combining strong classification performance with a consistently low false alert rate, thereby validating the proposed method for intrusion analysis studies. • Generation of packet-level datasets from independently built virtual and physical network environments • Optimization-driven feature selection using Particle Swarm Optimization to reduce redundancy • Cross-model evaluation of optimized classifiers, demonstrating superior reliability of the PSO-enhanced neural approach.

title: A novel intrusion detection system for dew computing environments based on an enhanced federated deep learning model
A Weighted Fusion Machine Learning Approach for Intrusion Detection in the Internet of Things
abstract: The continuous advancement of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has increased security vulnerabilities, highlighting the need for efficient Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Traditional ML-based IDS are lightweight but less robust, while DL-based methods offer higher accuracy but demand significant resources, limiting their suitability for IoT. To address this challenge, we propose a weighted fusion IDS combining Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest (RF). This fusion approach leverages the complementary strengths of the three algorithms, enhancing detection accuracy while maintaining efficiency. The model was evaluated on NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, ToN-IoT Windows 7, and ToN-IoT Windows 10 datasets, achieving accuracies of 99.27%, 79.36%, 100%, and 99.96%, respectively.

title: Explainable BiLSTM-MHA-Based IDS for IoT Using SHAP and Zero-Day Attack Detection
abstract: Because of their distributed nature, resource limitations, and the growing sophistication of cyberthreats, Internet of Things (IoT) environments pose serious security issues. The heterogeneity of devices and the vast volume of data they generate make IoT networks particularly vulnerable to a wide range of attacks, posing serious risks to privacy, safety, and critical infrastructure. This paper presents a new intrusion detection system (IDS) architecture utilizing bidirectional long short-term memory with multi-head attention (BiLSTM-MHA) to improve the detection of cyberattacks in IoT networks. The model was trained and evaluated using the comprehensive TON IoT dataset, encompassing multiple attack classes and normal traffic. Our approach achieved a high accuracy of 98.79%, a low loss of 0.0349, and a false positive rate (FPR) of just 0.0391%, while maintaining an efficient inference time of 0.002 seconds per instance, rendering it appropriate for real-time implementation in IoT systems. To mitigate the issue of class imbalance, the Focal Loss technique was employed, yielding superior performance compared to the baseline model trained on the imbalanced dataset. Furthermore, to enhance model transparency and interpretability, Explainable AI (XAI) methods were integrated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), enabling a detailed interpretation of the model’s decision-making process and the identification of the most influential features associated with each attack class. This provided deeper insights into the model’s behavior and validated the importance of key features in detecting different intrusion types. We further evaluated the model’s generalization capability through a Zero-Day attack assessment using a Leave-One-Attack-Out (LOAO) strategy. The model was trained without one attack class and tested on that unseen class to simulate a realistic zero-day scenario. It achieved a testing accuracy of 97.91%, a loss of 0.0591, and an F1-score of 98.94%, confirming its robustness and adaptability to unknown threats.

title: Research on Vehicle Speed Estimation Based on In-Vehicle Smartphone and 1D CNN-LSTN Network
DDoS Attack Detection in IoT Using Motion Behavior and Deep Learning
venue: IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) network based devices has increased the vulnerability to Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, creating a need for fast and intelligent detection frameworks. A performance-driven assessment is presented for a lightweight DDoS detection strategy that harnesses the capabilities of machine learning. The proposed system is benchmarked against recent advanced techniques, including IMD-Blockchain, DAS-ML, and TL-CNN-IDS. Key evaluation indicators such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, False Acceptance Rate (FAR), False Rejection Rate (FRR), and Latency are utilized to measure robustness, reliability, and efficiency. Experimental findings reveal that the proposed framework consistently outperforms existing methods by delivering higher detection accuracy, fewer false alarms, and reduced processing time, making it highly applicable for real-time deployment in resource-limited IoT settings. Furthermore, this research underscores the promise of adaptive ML-driven DDoS detection solutions in safeguarding IoT networks, providing a scalable, precise, and low-latency defense mechanism to counter evolving cyber threats in smart and interconnected environments.

title: Multiscale attention-based deep learning approach for ransomware threats detection and prevention
venue: Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation
abstract: In this research work, a new deep learning-based ransomware threat detection and prevention model is developed to protect the files in digital computing devices. Initially, essential data is collected from benchmark sources, and it is then subjected to the feature extraction phase, where Statistical features, Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-based features, and deep features are extracted. In addition, optimal features are selected using Enhanced Arbitrary Variable-based Nuclear Reaction Optimization (EAV-NRO). Finally, the extracted ensemble features are fed into the designed Multiscale Attention-based Residual Long Short-Term Memory (MA-ResLSTM) model to perform ransomware threat detection. The efficacy of the developed mechanism is verified among different state-of-the-art approaches. In dataset 1, the developed MA-ResLSTM approach attained 93.5% accuracy and 93.46% sensitivity, which is better than MLP, GAN, RNN and dual-layer RF. Thus, the outcome proved that the accurate detection of developed ransomware attack frameworks ensures that real threats are identified and mitigated properly.

title: An Deep Ensemble Learning Model with Metaheuristic Hyperparameter Optimization for Smart Grid Intrusion Detection
venue: Journal of Network and Systems Management

title: Machine Learning Models Accuracy Study Using P4 Programmable Data Plane in SDN - IOT Networks
abstract: Programmable data plane is the current trending area of research in networking. P4 is a programming language is using to handle different issues in data plane such as flow management, traffic management, and firewall management. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack is one of the crucial attacks in the network. Handling DDoS attacks at router level give more security to the network. This paper explores how the attack detection can be handled at router level in SDN-IoT Network. The proposed paper analyzes three different machine learning algorithms such as Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, and Tsetline Machine models on programmable data plane. Each machine learning model is implemented in a P4 programmable data plane environment using the BMv2 behavioral model and tested on a Mininet test-bed. The models uses the standard IoT data set of ICMP-based DDOS traffic features. The analysis explores the accuracy, memory efficiency, and feasibility for real-time deployment. The study proves that, novel adaptation of the Tsetlin Machine model into P4 logic, demonstrating its effectiveness and practicality for next-generation programmable networks.

title: Optimized Autoencoder for Intrusion Detection Systems
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) network intrusion detection system (IDS) is very difficult due to enormous amounts of data, device heterogeneity, and ever-evolving cyber threats. To cope with these challenges, a new hybrid IDS model that combines (AE) based deep feature extraction and the Beluga Whale Optimization Algorithm (BWOA) is introduced in this work. Preprocessing of the Bot-IoT dataset occurs prior to modeling involving cleaning, normalization, encoding, and class balancing for high-quality input. The$\mathbf{A E}$is used to learn meaningful latent features from dense network traffic for both feature learning and classification. To further boost detection performance, BWOA is utilized to adjust the AE's hyper parameters and optimize the classification thresholds. This combined solution greatly improves detection accuracy as well as system robustness. The experimental results verify the adaptability and scalability of the model for IDS in IoT networks in modern applications.

title: Deep learning models for intrusion detection of irregularities and security breach detection in 5G networks
Stacking-Based Deep Ensemble Framework for Robust DDoS Intrusion Detection
abstract: This paper presents an advanced intrusion detection system for Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks using ensemble learning. While most existing research in this field has focused on individual models, we combine multiple deep learning models through ensemble techniques to achieve superior performance. The base models employed are Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), which are integrated using simple averaging, weighted averaging, and stacking methods. Experiments are conducted on the CICDDoS2019 dataset, with the stacking ensemble delivering the best performance. The proposed model achieves an accuracy, precision, and recall of 97.30 %, along with an$\mathbf{F 1}$-score of 97.05 %. Furthermore, class imbalance is effectively addressed through weighted sampling.

title: SAINT-PBT: An Attention-Driven Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Cybersecurity Threat Severity Classification
abstract: The exponential growth in cybersecurity attacks is one of the greatest threats to the global digital infrastructure, challenging intelligent and adaptive detection mechanisms. This paper proposes a novel cyberattack categorization framework using a SAINT (Self-Attention and Intersample Attention Transformer) -based architecture, designed for very high accuracy and low computation on large-scale security data. Using the Global Cybersecurity Threats 2015-2024 dataset, the framework classifies the six most common attack types: Phishing, Ransomware, Man-in-the-Middle, Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS), SQL Injection, and Malware. The approach involves strong preprocessing in the form of categorical encoding, numerical normalization, and class imbalance treatment, followed by an SAINT-based deep learning model. To enhance model adaptability and performance, Population-Based Training (PBT) is proposed to conduct dynamic hyperparameter adjustment, such as Parameters like learning rate, attention heads, and embedding dimensions during training. Experimental outcomes show increased classification accuracy, recall, and precision over baseline deep learning practices, especially in highly imbalanced class scenarios. The proposed method's attention mechanism effectively learns intra- and inter-feature relationships and facilitates the efficient identification of sophisticated attack patterns in various sectors. The design can be adopted in real-time intrusion detection in cybersecurity monitoring systems for enhancing resilience against adaptive threats while being scalable for large-scale security operations globally.

title: An Encoder-Only Transformer with Features-as-Tokens for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
venue: International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
abstract: Modern intrusion detection systems increasingly rely on machine learning models that can handle heterogeneous flow features, severe class imbalance, and evolving network traffic. While prior Transformer-based IDS approaches have shown promise, many suffer from evaluation issues such as temporal leakage and insufficient handling of extreme class imbalance. This work introduces a comprehensive framework that combines a strictly leak-free evaluation protocol with an encoder-only Transformer that treats flow features as tokens, enabling the model to capture cross-feature interactions while remaining lightweight and deployment-friendly. The architecture incorporates a learnable feature-gating tokenizer and attention-based pooling, trained within a pipeline that uses time-aware splits, train-only preprocessing, robust imputation, outlier handling, and quantile-based scaling. Training stability and generalization are further improved through mixup regularization, a One-Cycle learning-rate schedule, stochastic weight averaging, and a focal-style loss for imbalanced data.On the CICIDS2017 benchmark, the proposed Transformer achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.99986, a PR-AUC of 0.99944, an accuracy of 0.9978, and an F1-score of 0.9943 for binary intrusion detection. In the more challenging 15-class setting, it attains an accuracy of 0.9977 and a macro F1-score of 0.6939, with strong performance on frequent attack categories. The model demonstrates competitive performance compared to traditional tree-based methods while maintaining exceptional computational efficiency with only 354K parameters and 0.0087ms inference latency per flow. An ablation study confirms the contribution of each pipeline component to overall robustness.

title: A Transformer-Based Intrusion Detection System with Attention-Driven Feature Selection for Network Traffic Classification
abstract: As cyber threats advance, conventional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) frequently face challenges in identifying emerging attacks owing to their dependence on manual feature extraction. The envisioned work enforces an enhanced transformer-based intrusion detection system with an attentiondriven feature selection. The Transformer Encoder uses a multi-head self-attention mechanism to capture intricate dependencies in network traffic competently. After that, a lightweight classifier is used to detect intrusions using the cultivated representations. The implemented model demonstrates outstanding performance on the UNSW-NB15 dataset, effectively addressing class imbalance and accurately identifying attacks, achieving an accuracy of 95.68%, precision of 96.42%, recall of 95.70%, and an$\mathbf{F 1}$-score of 96.06%. The two preprocessing strategies, i.e., Z -score normalisation and categorical encoding, are utilised to upgrade detection competence and model sturdiness.

title: An Efficient IoT Security Prediction Framework
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is widely used in modern industrial applications due to its inherent capability of transferring data without human intervention. A Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) is the central part and plays an important role in IoT. These are widely used in complex applications in which various security attacks are encountered to prevent and countermeasure the problems in WSN, such as data processing, analysis, and efficient utilization of network resources. To ensure secure data processing, techniques are proposed to protect data privacy. Therefore, we propose a novel data-driven model using the benchmark NSL-KDD dataset based on a randomized tree, which improves the performance of WSNs. The performance analysis of the proposed model has been analyzed by using different metrics, e.g., RMSE, MSE, MAE, R-Squared, training time, model size, and prediction speed. The results obtained in the experiments depict that the proposed model effectively performs better than other contemporary models in the state of the art in case of different errors such as RMSE, MSE, MAE, R-Squared, etc.

title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Approaches to Cybersecurity in Internet of Things Manufacturing Systems and a Deep Hybrid Learning Framework for Malware Detection
venue: Journal of Manufacturing Science and Engineering
abstract: Abstract Cyberattacks have been rising steadily since the 1990s, and today the manufacturing and industrial sectors have become prime targets. U.S. manufacturing is seen as a lucrative target because of its rich space for exploitation, the fear of production halts, and the lack of a reliable, self-sufficient supply chain that can support operations during crises. With the growing use of interconnected technologies, entry points for attackers are more numerous than ever. Traditional methods such as signature-based or static defenses have proven ineffective, while artificial intelligence (AI)-driven approaches have shown promise but often lack consistency, performing well in some areas while failing in others. This study addresses that challenge by examining existing AI models used for cyber-threat detection, evaluating their advantages and limitations, and proposing a more reliable alternative. This article proposes a lightweight and easily deployable deep hybrid learning (DHL) model trained and tested on the TON_IoT dataset. The model was compared against ten of the most widely used machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models in cybersecurity and achieved superior performance with 98.13% accuracy, 98.82% precision, 98.24% recall, and 98.53% F1. This study provides practical recommendations to strengthen industrial systems and protect U.S. manufacturing enterprises from the growing wave of cyber threats.

title: Enhancing IoT Network Security Through an Advanced Deep Learning-Powered Threat Detection System
venue: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology Transactions of Electrical Engineering

title: XAI-IDS: DeepLIFT-AE driven granular feature extraction for intelligent detection of emerging vehicular network threats
abstract: The growing reliance on the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has intensified the need for robust Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), as recent studies reveal that over 60% of vehicular network breaches result from DoS and spoofing attacks, contributing to annual losses exceeding $1.2 billion globally. Despite advancements, conventional IDS frameworks still suffer from limited interpretability, high false alarm rates, and inadequate adaptability to evolving attack patterns. To address these challenges, this research introduces a novel eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based IDS framework utilizing the CICIoV-2024 dataset, which comprehensively represents real-time vehicular communication including Benign, DoS, and Spoofing traffic. The data undergoes rigorous preprocessing to remove noise and standardize features. A hybrid Fuzzy Probability Clustering with SHapley Additive Explanations (FPC-SHAP) is employed for granular feature extraction by estimating uncertainty and relevance simultaneously. Subsequently, DeepLIFT-Autoencoder (DeepLIFT-AE) is applied for feature ranking, capturing both low- and high-level semantic patterns. For classification, a Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations-based Globally Randomized Ensemble (LIME-GRE) model is implemented, enabling highly interpretable decision boundaries across the three attack classes. The proposed XAI-IDS method achieved excellent performance in the evaluation, with an Accuracy of 99.966% and a Precision of 99.987%. It also demonstrated strong results in Recall at 99.786% and an F1 Score of 99.886%, indicating highly effective classification, which are increased over state of art methodologies.

title: Graph Convolution Neural Network and Deep Q-Network Optimization-Based Intrusion Detection with Explainability Analysis
abstract: As networks expand in size and complexity, coupled with an exponential increase in intrusions on network and IoT systems, this leads to traditional models failing to capture increasingly intricate correlations among network components accurately. Graph Convolution Networks (GCNs) have recently acquired prominence for their capacity to represent nodes, edges, or entire graphs by aggregating information from adjacent nodes. However, the correlations between nodes and their neighbours, as well as related edges, differ. Assigning higher weights to nodes and edges with high similarity improves model accuracy and expressiveness. In this paper, we propose the GCN-DQN model, which integrates GCN with a multi-head attention mechanism and DQN (Deep Q Network) to adaptively adjust attention weights optimizing its performance in intrusion detection tasks. After extensive experiments using the UNSW NB15 and CIC-IDS2017 dataset, the proposed GCN-DQN outperformed the baseline model in classification accuracy. We also applied LIME and SHAP techniques to provide explainability to our proposed intrusion detection model.

title: SAE-CNN-LSTM-based anomaly detection and mitigation framework for cloud-centric SDN environments
venue: Journal of Cloud Computing Advances Systems and Applications
abstract: The advent of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) has transformed the landscape of cloud network management by decoupling the control and data planes, enabling centralized programmability and dynamic policy enforcement. However, this paradigm shift introduces new challenges for real-time anomaly detection and DDoS mitigation. This paper proposes an intelligent anomaly mitigation framework that leverages deep learning techniques—specifically Sparse Autoencoders (SAE) for feature extraction and a hybrid CNN-LSTM model for capturing both spatial and temporal traffic anomalies. The system is implemented and evaluated using Python 3.9 with TensorFlow 2.x on a Ryu SDN controller integrated with OpenFlow-based switches in Mininet. Experiments are conducted across various SDN topologies including Star, Mesh, Tree, and Random configurations. Benchmark datasets CIC-DDoS2019 and UNSW-NB15 are used for model training and validation. The proposed framework achieves 99.1% detection accuracy, a 30% improvement in false positive rate over traditional methods, and reduces mitigation time by up to 40%, confirming its suitability for real-time deployment in dynamic SDN environments.

title: Toward AI-driven IoT cybersecurity: A preprocessing framework for benchmark datasets
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, found in environments such as smart homes, poses growing cybersecurity challenges. In response, research has examined the role of artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning, in enhancing IoT security. To support this effort, machine learning models have been developed and evaluated on benchmark datasets. However, preparing datasets for machine learning requires preprocessing techniques that are tailored to the specific characteristics of the data. In this context, exploratory data analysis provides insights into dataset structure and distribution, thereby supporting informed preprocessing decisions prior to modeling. Accordingly, this study introduces a reproducible five‑step preprocessing framework for IoT cybersecurity datasets and demonstrates its application to the NF‑ToN‑IoT V1 dataset. The proposed framework is organized into two phases: an exploratory data analysis phase consisting of (1) dataset overview and identification of categorical and numerical features, (2) analysis of missing and zero values, (3) assessment of categorical feature distributions, and (4) assessment of numerical feature distributions; and a preprocessing phase consisting of (5) proportional stratified random downsampling to produce a reduced dataset that preserves the original class distribution. By establishing a systematic, data-driven framework, this study contributes to the preparation of structured datasets for attack detection in IoT environments, with potential applications in smart homes.

title: Emerging Paradigm of Quantum Machine Learning: Knowledge Insights and Future Prospects
abstract: The machines can handle tasks that require thinking and decisive capacity by using Artificial Intelligence. But these systems require higher resources for their operations. As such, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has been explored as a parallel solution for such problems. In our study, we comprehensively analyzed the research evolution within the QML domain. We integrated literature from Scopus and Web of Science to investigate underlying relationships through bibliometric information. The publication and citation trends, country collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic relationships helped to introspect the growth of QML. Our results show that quantum kernels, quantum natural language processing, contrastive learning, quantum reservoir computing, and explainable QML are gaining attention within academia. It has been expanding across a diverse set of problem spaces like management of resources, intrusion detection, process control, cloud computing, molecular and materials modeling, simulation of integrated circuits, and nuclear physics, etc. The findings also highlight the existing challenges that are limiting the practical implementation of solutions within the NISQ era. In response, we also identified actionable directives that can be followed for advancing the current state of research.
