title: Implement Federated Intelligence with Ensemble Stream Mining for Privacy-Aware and Collaborative Intrusion Detection in Distributed IoT Network Architectures
A Comparative Evaluation of Standalone and Hybrid Machine Learning Techniques for Network Anomaly Detection Using NSL-KDD
An LSTM-based intrusion detection model utilizing feature selection and dropout
abstract: With the advancement of network technology, cybersecurity concerns have intensified, as intrusions pose significant risks to both individuals and organizations. In order to solve the problem of low detection accuracy and high false alarm rate caused by redundant features in network traffic data, a new model is thus developed in this study for intrusion detection that employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to learn the temporal attributes of network traffic data, complemented by feature selection and dropout techniques, to enhance detection accuracy. The approach begins by applying the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm for feature selection on network traffic data, reducing feature redundancy. Consequently, the most relevant features are identified for effective classification. The selected features undergo preprocessing through one-hot encoding and normalization before being input into the LSTM network for training. To enhance performance, dropout is employed to minimize overfitting and boost generalization. When tested on the CICIDS2017, the model outperforms traditional methods such as convolutional neural network (CNN), Logistic Regression, and Bayesian models in binary as well as multi-class classification tasks. Significantly, this approach is particularly effective at detecting minority attack types, especially Web attack and Bot, in the multi-class classification.

title: CCA-ID: Confidence-calibrated adaptive intrusion detection with selective routing for IoT networks
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has extended the cyber-attack surface. In resource-constrained IoT monitoring environments, maintaining always-on deep or ensemble-based intrusion detection can be challenging for high-rate, real-time traffic. This study presents CCA-ID, Confidence Calibrated Adaptive Intrusion Detection which integrates calibrated decision confidence with selective, resource-aware inference for IoT intrusion detection. CCA-ID combines an isotonic-calibrated logistic regression gate, heterogeneous heavy learners including DNN, XGBoost, and LightGBM, and a stacking meta-classifier within a class-specific confidence-driven routing mechanism. High-confidence samples are finalized by the lightweight calibrated gate, whereas low-confidence samples are selectively routed to the heavy ensemble for deeper analysis. The proposed CCA-ID is evaluated on the large-scale Gotham Dataset 2025, using a final experimental dataset comprising 7,792,438 packet-level samples across 18 traffic classes. Experimental results indicate that CCA-ID achieves 89.92% accuracy, 61.70% macro F1-score, and 98.93% macro ROC-AUC, while routing only 6.28% of samples to the heavy ensemble. The method also achieves an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 7.66%, showing improved confidence reliability for routing decisions. An inference-time analysis further indicates that CCA-ID achieves a 13.94× speedup over the always-on heavy stack on a fixed stratified subset of the held-out test set. Overall, CCA-ID provides a calibrated trade-off between selective inference and heavy-model invocation for IoT intrusion detection. It reduces unnecessary heavy-model usage while maintaining strong threshold-free discriminative performance under severe class imbalance.

title: Enhanced Wireless Sensor Network Security Through Machine Learning-Based Data-Driven Intrusion Detection
A Secure and Parallel IoT Automation Architecture for Centralized Control of Multiple Computers
Graph Database-Augmented Temporal Fusion Transformer for Short-Term Load Forecasting: A Unified Spatial and Load-CorrelationGraph Approach
An enhanced cybersecurity testing based on CHSPNN and DG in software testing for banking or finance applications
venue: Communications in Statistics Case Studies Data Analysis and Applications
abstract: Cyber testing is very essential for banking or finance applications to test the software for the identification of cyber-attacks in the software codes. None of the existing work in financial software has covered layers such as network breaches, application layer attacks, and social engineering and insider threats for cyber-security testing. Therefore, the paper presents cyber-security testing in software testing, covering all these layers. Initially, the input software code is converted into a graphical representation using AST. From this, vectorization and patching is carried out by B-SMART and SRSKFC, followed by feature extraction. After the patching process, graph kernel analysis is done, and with the extracted features, both are given to feature selection performed by GSCLO to select the optimal features. Then, behavior analysis takes place, which consists of pre-processing the data, and from this data, features are extracted. Now, extracted features and selected optimal features are given to CHSPNN classifier. Finally, from the obtained class the attacked surface in the code is mapped using DG. Hence, the proposed model is classified and the attacks are mapped very effectively, with an accuracy of 97.97%.

title: Cross-dataset zero-shot IoT attack detection using a hybrid CNN–BiLSTM + attention framework with explainable AI
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has heightened network susceptibility to diverse cyber-attacks and volumetric threats. Conventional intrusion detection systems (IDS) often struggle to generalise across heterogeneous network environments due to unstandardised feature spaces, distribution shifts, and an inability to capture complementary spatial and recurrent feature representations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an attention-gated hybrid CNN–BiLSTM deep learning framework for robust, interpretable cross-dataset zero-shot IoT attack detection. The architecture integrates parallel 1D-CNN spatial filtering and BiLSTM feature-channel encoding, an attention-based feature-gating layer for dynamic representation refinement, a common preprocessing protocol with dataset-specific feature representations for leak-free flow representations, and a multi-level explainable AI (XAI) framework combining SHAP, LIME, and ANOVA. Evaluated across five independent random seeds on four benchmark datasets (Apose-IoT-23, BoT-IoT, CIC-IoMT-2024, and CIC-IoT-2025) under a leakage-free 70%:15%:15% split, the framework achieves mean binary classification accuracies of 99.33%, 99.997%, 99.83%, and 98.73%, with macro-averaged F1-scores of 99.15%, 94.68%, 97.90%, and 98.70%, respectively. In multiclass threat scenarios, the model maintains high accuracy (98.86%, 99.74%, 99.21%, and 97.61%) and macro F1-scores up to 96.29%. Furthermore, zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation assesses out-of-distribution transferability across heterogeneous IoT topologies and protocol stacks using a deterministic dimensional adaptation operator. Tiered XAI interpretations provide complementary global and local feature attribution transparency, while GPU efficiency benchmarking demonstrates low amortised per-sample batch inference latencies (0.0123–0.0160 ms/sample), establishing a solid empirical foundation for future hardware-based edge security deployment.

title: Intrusion Detection With Machine and Deep Learning: A Comparative Study on CICIDS‐2017 and NSL‐KDD
abstract: ABSTRACT With the rapid advancement of technology, the complexity and frequency of cyberattacks are increasing, necessitating advanced defensive measures. Intrusion detection systems (IDS) play a critical role in mitigating these threats. This study investigates the effectiveness of diverse algorithmic architectures—including Machine Learning (ML) (Random Forest, Decision Tree [DT], KNN), Deep Learning (DL) (CNN, DNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, GRU, BiGRU), and Hybrid models (CNN+BiLSTM, GRU+Random Forest)—using the NSL‐KDD and CICIDS‐2017 datasets as established benchmark datasets. To optimize performance, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and SelectKBest + Mutual Information (SKB+MI) were applied for feature selection. Experimental results show that while the DT algorithm achieved a peak accuracy of 99% on the CICIDS‐2017 dataset, it demonstrated sensitivity to dataset‐specific artifacts. In contrast, the GRU+Random Forest hybrid model demonstrated favorable performance and operational efficiency, achieving a testing latency of 0.03 s. This research provides a comparative framework for examining the trade‐off between detection precision and computational overhead, offering insights into cross‐dataset generalizability and potential deployment considerations for high‐throughput network environments.

title: A two-stage deep learning approach for multiclass DGA-based malware communication detection and classification in DoH network traffic
abstract: The adoption of DNS over HTTPS (DoH) has substantially improved user privacy by encrypting DNS queries, but it has also introduced new opportunities for attackers to hide Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA)-based malware communications. In this study, we propose a novel two-stage deep learning framework that integrates an Autoencoder (AE) with Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for detecting and classifying DGA-based malware in DoH traffic. The first stage employs an AE for dimensionality reduction and optimal feature extraction, followed by hybrid feature selection combining Random Forest (RF) importance scores and Mutual Information (MI). The second stage utilizes LSTM and GRU for binary and multiclass classification of malware families. To ensure robust evaluation, we employed stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 5) and applied temporal SMOTE (tSMOTE) to training data to address class imbalance while avoiding data leakage. The proposed framework was evaluated on the CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 and DoH-DGA-Malware-Traffic-HKD datasets. AE-LSTM achieves 0.9958 accuracy for binary classification, while AE-GRU attains 0.9925 accuracy for multiclass classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively identifies DGA-based malware in encrypted DoH traffic and outperforms standalone models across most evaluation metrics.

title: Parallel Local–Global Feature Extraction and Cross-Attention Gated Fusion for Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: With the rapid advancement of network technology and the Internet of Things (IoT), massive, high-dimensional traffic data pose significant challenges to Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS). Existing deep learning methods face two major limitations: (1) Insufficient feature extraction: single models struggle to concurrently capture local and global features, while serial hybrid architectures are prone to feature information loss. (2) Superficial feature fusion: existing strategies overlook deep interactions between features and lack adaptive filtering mechanisms to eliminate redundant information. To address these issues, a Parallel Local-Global Feature Extraction (PLGFE) module is constructed, incorporating a dual-stream architecture with parallel Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) branches. This module utilizes TCN's dilated convolutions and BiLSTM's bidirectional memory units to concurrently extract complementary local and global features. The Cross-Attention Gating (CAG) module integrates cross-attention and gating mechanisms for feature fusion: the former enables deep interaction between heterogeneous features, while the latter adaptively selects key features and suppresses redundant interaction features through gated weights. Experiments on the CICIDS2017 and CICIoV2024 datasets demonstrate the proposed method achieves multi-classification accuracies of 99.85% and 99.64%, with F1-Scores of 97.03% and 97.64%, respectively. Comparisons and ablation experiments confirm its competitive detection performance and component effectiveness.

title: DAD-EMGNN: Detecting Anomalous Database User Behavior via Feature-Enhanced Multiplexed Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Existing methods for structured database anomaly access detection focus on the content of SQL operation statements, scoring each operation in isolation while neglecting the relational structure among operations. We propose DAD-EMGNN (Data-user Anomaly Detection via Enhanced Multiplexed Graph Neural Networks), an unsupervised framework that abstracts each database operation as a graph node and links operations sharing a value on any of ten operational metadata fields, such as session identifier, client port, and request time zone, forming a Multiplexed Graph Neural Network (MGNN). The framework is organized as six loosely coupled stages with explicit interfaces, so that components can be validated, replaced, or ablated independently. Three innovations distinguish this work: BERT-based node attribute encoding that captures the syntactic and semantic properties of SQL statements; K-Core graph enhancement that concentrates information at structurally important nodes; and a Graph Transformer Encoder paired with a Graph Transformer Discriminator, which together yield richer consensus embeddings and pseudo-label-guided attack identification without labeled samples. We further construct Dataset-D, containing 7,000 operation records spanning 21 attack types. DAD-EMGNN achieves NMI = 0.4287, Accuracy = 86.31%, and F1 = 0.8599, surpassing all baselines, and supplementary experiments on three public graph benchmarks validate its generalization.

title: QuadFusion-IDS: Enhancing Intrusion Detection with Unified Hybrid Deep and Machine Learning Techniques in Cybersecurity Systems
abstract: As network traffic becomes increasingly complex and cyberattack behaviors continue to evolve, conventional intrusion detection approaches face challenges in accurately identifying malicious and legitimate network activities. This study proposes QuadFusion-IDS, a hybrid binary intrusion detection framework that integrates FT-Transformer with Autoencoder (FT-Transformer + AE), multi-head attention deep neural network (MHA-DNN), dilated temporal convolutional network (Dilated TCN), and XGBoost to capture complementary feature representations, temporal dependencies, and nonlinear traffic patterns. The framework employs a controlled preprocessing pipeline involving categorical encoding, variance-based filtering, correlation analysis, Random Forest-based feature selection, normalization, stratified train-validation-test partitioning, and ADASYN-based class balancing, while maintaining a locked test set to minimize information leakage. Using the UNSW-NB15 dataset, QuadFusion-IDS achieved an accuracy of 0.9545, a precision of 0.9566, a recall of 0.9775, an F1-score of 0.9669, an MCC of 0.8946, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9922 for binary classification of normal and attack traffic. Ablation experiments demonstrated the importance of ensemble components and optimized weighting, with XGBoost removal producing the largest reduction in F1-score and AUC-ROC. Multi-seed evaluation further showed small performance variations, supporting the stability of the proposed framework. Feature selection analysis indicated that the selected 20-feature configuration substantially reduces input dimensionality while retaining competitive detection performance compared with the original 42-feature configuration. SHAP and LIME analyses provide feature-level and local decision explanations for network traffic predictions. Overall, QuadFusion-IDS provides a strong and interpretable binary intrusion detection approach for the UNSW-NB15 benchmark, while further validation under live traffic, adversarial conditions, streaming workloads, and operational cybersecurity environments remains necessary.

title: CRISPR-AF: A Bio-Inspired Adaptive Firewall with Self-Curating Signature Memory for Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: Exact-match intrusion detection systems like Snort keep adding rules and rarely retire them, so over time firewalls waste effort scanning thousands of expired signatures in every packet. A small change to a payload is often enough to slip past these strict patterns. Bacteria handle the same problem differently. Their CRISPR-Cas immune system keeps no endless log of past infections, only a small, current set of viral snippets that it forgets once the threat fades. CRISPR-AF applies this idea. It is a self-learning firewall that keeps a tightly-bounded array of short signatures and catches altered payloads by approximate matching. It adds signatures during attacks and drops ones that stop matching, so the rule set never grows without bound. On CICIDS2017, it matched Random Forest, a deep neural network, and a traditional Artificial Immune System using only a fraction of the rules, resisted polymorphic attacks, and learned new attacks without retraining.

title: MOS-IDS: Detecting and Characterizing Unknown Attacks in Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment via Multimodal Open-Set Learning
abstract: Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) represents a critical infrastructure increasingly exposed to sophisticated cyberattacks. Existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) rely on closed-set assumptions, making them unable to handle unknown attack types at runtime. Current unimodal and closed-set approaches fail to generalize beyond their training distribution, leaving EVSE networks vulnerable to novel threats. In this paper, we propose MOS-IDS, a Multimodal Open-Set Intrusion Detection System that fuses Network and Kernel modalities through independent autoencoders into a unified 64-dimensional latent representation. MOS-IDS operates in three phases: anomaly detection via Isolation Forest, attack Classification using a Conv1D neural network with OpenMax open-set recognition, and unknown threat characterization based on Mahalanobis distance. Experimental results demonstrate that MOS-IDS achieves high detection accuracy on known attacks while effectively identifying unknown samples and distinguishing novel threats from boundary noise. MOS-IDS provides a robust and flexible detection framework for EVSE security, making it suitable for deployment across distributed charging networks.

title: A review of lightweight intrusion detection and security mechanisms for resource constrained IoT and WSNs
abstract: Resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices and wireless sensor networks (WSNs) remain difficult to secure using conventional security mechanisms because their sensing, forwarding, and processing nodes operate with limited memory, computation, energy, bandwidth, and software-update capability. These limits expose constrained deployments to attacks on end nodes, routing paths, wireless links, and sensed data. Recent research has therefore proposed lightweight intrusion detection (IDS) and protection methods that reduce input dimensionality, model size, computation, communication overhead, authentication cost, or energy use. The literature, however, remains uneven in how it defines lightweightness, relates lightweight design to security risk, and demonstrates deployability under constrained operation. This article reviews recent lightweight security risk analysis and IDS research for constrained IoT and WSN systems, with emphasis on studies published from 2023 to 2026. It examines feature selection, compact machine learning, compressed deep learning, TinyML, edge-assisted detection, federated learning, lightweight authentication, trust-based scoring, cryptography, and energy-aware routing. The review compares technique families, attack coverage, resource-efficiency evidence, datasets, metrics, and reporting practices. It also separates IoT and WSN assumptions because IoT IDS papers often rely on flow datasets and edge deployment, whereas WSN studies more often address routing attacks, energy depletion, topology instability, and node compromise. The main contribution is a resource-aware taxonomy and comparative evaluation framework that separate lightweight security claims from deployment evidence, clarify IoT and WSN evaluation assumptions, and identify the minimum reporting requirements needed to judge operational feasibility. The reviewed studies indicate that resource metrics should be treated as primary evaluation outcomes and that lightweight security must be assessed through the joint assessment of detection quality, risk reduction, and operational feasibility.

title: Sequential machine learning for intrusion detection in imbalanced cloud-oriented network traffic
abstract: Intrusion detection in cloud-oriented network environments remains challenging because of heterogeneous traffic patterns, natural class imbalance, noisy observations, and evolving attack behaviors. This study presents a lightweight hybrid soft-computing framework structured as a sequential learning pipeline that combines X-Means clustering, Isolation Forest, and XGBoost. The proposed design explicitly coordinates three complementary stages: adaptive feature-space organization, class-aware anomaly filtering, and multiclass discrimination. X-Means groups features adaptively and retains representative variables without requiring a predefined number of clusters. Isolation Forest is applied in a class-aware manner to filter irregular majority-class observations while preserving minority-class samples. XGBoost then performs the final intrusion classification on the refined representation. The framework is evaluated on four benchmark datasets, namely CICIDS-2017, CIC-IDS-Collection, NSL-KDD, and UNSW-NB15, under natural class-imbalance conditions without synthetic oversampling. The results demonstrate strong detection capability across the heterogeneous traffic distributions considered in this study. Overall accuracies reach 99.87% on CICIDS-2017 and 99.71% on NSL-KDD, while remaining competitive on more challenging benchmarks. A global ablation study confirms that performance gains result from the coordinated interaction of the individual stages rather than from the isolated use of a strong classifier. Additional analyses, including feature-selection comparison, contamination-rate sensitivity, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)-based interpretability, and runtime measurement, provide a broader assessment of the pipeline. These findings indicate that the proposed framework offers a favorable compromise between predictive performance, robustness, interpretability, and computational efficiency. This highlights the relevance of lightweight, sequential hybrid soft-computing for scalable intrusion detection in naturally imbalanced cloud environments.

title: Adaptive Deep Neural Network Method for Engineering Structural Reliability Analysis with Imbalanced Samples
abstract: To improve the accuracy and efficiency of engineering structural reliability analysis under imbalanced sample conditions, an adaptive deep neural network (ADNN) method is pro-posed. The method integrates limit state surface (LSS)-based stratified splitting, a composite loss function, and an adaptive training strategy into the DNN framework. In the proposed method, the DNN is employed to establish the mapping relationship between input variables and output responses. The LSS-based stratified splitting improves the representativeness of samples near the LSS; the composite loss function assigns greater importance to samples in critical regions, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to learn the LSS; and the adaptive training strategy is used to improve model robustness. The proposed method is validated through two nonlinear function examples and a cable-stayed bridge engineering example, in which the failure-sample proportions in the model-construction datasets range from 0.10 to 0.33. The results show that ADNN improves the approximation capability of the LSS and maintains good reliability analysis performance as the failure-sample proportion decreases. Compared with conventional surrogate models, the ADNN method achieves higher accuracy and efficiency in reliability analysis. This study provides methodological support for structural reliability analysis under imbalanced sample conditions.

title: ASIF: A Resource-Aware Selective Network Traffic Inspection Framework Integrating Certificate Screening, Targeted Decryption, and Feature Fusion
abstract: The widespread use of TLS in IoT and networked systems increases inspection cost while restricting direct access to payload content. This paper presents the Adaptive Secure Inspection Framework (ASIF), a resource-aware selective network traffic inspection framework that coordinates certificate-based routing, authorized targeted decryption, known-signature matching, and learned flow classification. ASIF contains three components: (1) a Certificate Screening Module (CSM), which applies configured checks of root trust, chain integrity, and leaf-certificate validity as an early routing signal; (2) a Targeted Decryption and Signature Matching Module (TDSMM), which directs certificate-suspicious traffic to authorized Mitmproxy interception and Snort inspection; and (3) an Attentive Feature Fusion Network (AFFN), which combines global and local representations for network-flow classification. The evaluation covers controlled certificate cases, selective-decryption overhead, known-signature matching, learned classification on three intrusion datasets, a supplementary VPN/non-VPN task, held-out attack families, and the integrated pipeline. The intrusion-dataset labels do not establish that every flow is encrypted. Several models obtain near-ceiling scores under the balanced grouped protocol, while AFFN achieves a macro-F1 of 0.639 ± 0.149 on the supplementary ISCX VPN/non-VPN task and does not outperform all baselines. Across held-out attack families, recall averages 0.527 ± 0.466, indicating strong family dependence. In the controlled end-to-end experiment, complete ASIF decrypts 50% of requests and reduces mean latency from 278.78 to 164.19 ms/request relative to full decryption, while malicious-class recall decreases to 0.500 and macro-F1 to 0.733 because valid-certificate malicious traffic bypasses deeper inspection. These results characterize ASIF as a resource-aware selective inspection strategy with explicit coverage limitations rather than a universal encrypted-malicious-traffic detector.

Fine-Grained IoT Attack Classification Using a Cross-Attention CNN-BiLSTM Model
abstract: Deep learning intrusion detection systems perform well when traffic is merely separated into normal and malicious, but fine-grained recognition of the specific attack family remains difficult in Internet of Things (IoT) environments because of severe class imbalance and overlapping feature distributions. This work proposes an attention-enhanced CNN-BiLSTM fusion model for the multi-class classification of IoT attacks over eight families. A convolutional branch extracts local feature interactions, whereas a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) branch reads the standardized flow descriptor as an ordered sequence and encodes dependencies among non-adjacent feature segments in both directions. Multi-head self-attention and a bidirectional cross-attention block let the two representations interact dynamically and suppress redundant information. Class imbalance is addressed with a focal loss and class-balanced weighting. The framework was evaluated on the large-scale CIC-IoT2023 benchmark under an eight-class taxonomy. On more than 3.5 × 105 test flows, the proposed model reached 99.06% accuracy and a 98.99% weighted F1-score, outperforming standalone CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, and CNN-BiLSTM baselines retrained on the same corrected data pipeline under an identical objective and budget.

title: Hard-label black-box model extraction attacks against network intrusion detection systems via generative adversarial networks
venue: Journal of Information Security and Applications
abstract: Machine-learning-based network intrusion detection systems (ML-NIDS) are now widely deployed as security services, yet they remain vulnerable to model extraction. Prior work typically relies on the soft-label confidence scores of the victim, whereas ML-NIDS in production usually return only the Top-1 prediction. Network traffic is also tabular and severely class-imbalanced, so techniques developed for image models do not transfer directly. We show that diverse ML-NIDS can be cloned with high fidelity from hard-label queries combined with a small proxy set, without any internal information or confidence scores. To this end, we propose a framework that jointly trains a clone model and a sample generator, so that the generator produces informative queries and adapts to the characteristics of tabular network data. The framework further stabilizes training and preserves high extraction quality on rare attack classes, which are easily degraded under conventional optimization. We evaluate the attack under realistic black-box conditions on NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and CSE-CIC-IDS2018, including a cross-dataset distribution shift. Across five architecturally distinct ML-NIDS on CIC-IDS2017, it attains 82–99% Mean Per-Class Fidelity under a limited query budget, showing that restricting API outputs to Top-1 predictions alone is insufficient to protect deployed ML-NIDS against model extraction.

title: Robust multi-class DDoS and fraud detection using a Context-Adaptive Deep Evolutionary Game Framework with CNN–BiGRU
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks have become a serious threat in modern computer networks, which can commonly be integrated with other types of attacks to evade detection by conventional devices. Existing deep learning-based intrusion detection methods have high identification capability. However, they are also highly susceptible to adversarial attacks, in which even slight perturbations to features can fool the model into misclassification. To address these issues, this study introduced a hybrid deep learning framework. It integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU) to detect diverse types of attacks in real time. CNN extracts spatial interactions to model traffic characteristics, while BiGRU, a recurrent neural network, models temporal dependencies in data flows. This combination enables the model to capture complex spatiotemporal behavioral patterns in network traffic. To address class imbalance, we propose a new Neuro-Evolutionary Resampling Algorithm (NERA). This method uses neural density estimation and evolutionary optimization to generate balanced, noise-filtered training samples. Additionally, a Context-Adaptive Deep Evolutionary Game Framework (CADEGF) is designed to improve resistance to attacks. It does this by simulating interactions between attackers and defenders. It also adjusts detection thresholds using game-theoretic ideas. Experimental results show that this approach achieves high classification accuracy, effectively detects minority classes, and highlights trade-offs between minority-class detection and adversarial robustness, indicating contexts where NERA benefits or harms resilience. The integrated synergy of NERA, CNN-BiGRU, and CADEGF establishes a context-aware, adaptive defense model that advances intelligent intrusion detection with balanced performance and adversarial robustness.

title: Deep Learning Approaches for Intrusion Detection System Using Multi-Model Architectures for Network Security
venue: Sakarya University Journal of Computer and Information Sciences
abstract: It has become necessary to design efficient, robust, and effective Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) amid the rising complexity of cyberattacks and the exponential growth in network traffic. In this work, we present an advanced IDS framework using comparative deep learning (in short, DL) models for precise classification and detection of all types of network intrusions. The proposed system consists of five DL models: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and a Transformer-based model, which are trained and tested on the CICIDS2017 and CICIDS2018 datasets, whose network characteristics are close to real-world network traces. The Input features were pre-processed with data encoding and standardization to facilitate and make them compatible with optimal learning for models. The dataset was split into a 70% training set and a 30% test set to evaluate the generalization of the models. We used F1 score, recall, precision, and accuracy as metrics to evaluate the performance. The convolutional models, especially the 1DCNN, perform better due to the feature extraction using convolutions, achieving 99.20%, while LSTM achieved 98.68% and RNN 98.53%. These findings are further indicative of the potential that DL-based hybrid frameworks present for developing an intelligent, scalable, and time-sensitive IDS enabling practical applicability.

title: AI-Driven Intrusion Detection for Vehicular Networks: A Comprehensive Survey of Techniques, Datasets, Deployment Architectures, and Future Directions
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems (ITSs), Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication and autonomous driving technologies have brought about significant changes in the modern vehicular network. At the same time, the cyber-attack surface has grown, leading to new and existing advanced security threats for Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs) and the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Traditional IDSs that employ static rule-based techniques are often insufficient in the context of the vehicular environment, characterized by dynamic, highly mobile systems with stringent low-latency requirements. Next generation IDS development has shifted to artificial intelligence (AI), which offers adaptive, scalable and data-driven detection capabilities. In this survey, the authors present a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art of AI-driven vehicle IDS in terms of machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), federated learning (FL), reinforcement learning (RL), transformer-based techniques, and graph neural network (GNN) designs. We present a multidimensional taxonomy of vehicular attacks, an analysis of existing datasets and their weaknesses, an evaluation of the performance of AI techniques and a study of potential deployment architectures such as edge, fog and cloud. Furthermore, some of the most important open problems are identified, including data scarcity, adversarial robustness, real-time constraints, data utility-privacy conflicts, and standardization gaps. A research roadmap is provided, including 6G connectivity, blockchain-based IDS, explainable AI (XAI), Digital Twin technologies and post-quantum cryptography. This survey provides a common reference for the designers and developers of secure, efficient and interoperable VIDSs.

title: Deep Defender: An Adaptive Edge Cloud Framework for Intelligent DDoS Detection, Deception, and Tracking
abstract: Cloud computing environments are increasingly vulnerable to Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks and sophisticated cyber intrusions that compromise service availability, scalability, and operational security. In this research, we have developed a resilient cloud-based intrusion detection framework using a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) deep-learning architecture for intelligent DDoS detection and cyberattack tracking. The proposed framework integrates spatial feature extraction and temporal traffic-learning mechanisms to effectively capture complex network-behavior patterns within heterogeneous cloud environments. We used the NSL-KDD dataset for experimental validation, which included preprocessing, feature normalization, correlation analysis, feature-importance evaluation, PCA visualization, and t-SNE-based nonlinear traffic analysis. The results reflected high detection performance (accuracy-99.14%, precision-99.06%, recall-99.14%, and F1 score-99.04%) besides low false-positive behavior and strong attack-prediction. The developed framework exhibited robust adaptive intrusion-learning capability, reliable multi-class attack classification, and scalable operational suitability for intelligent cloud-security monitoring and resilient cyber-threat management applications.

Dual-Time-Scale Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Message-Budgeted Network Flow Intrusion Detection
abstract: Graph-based network intrusion detection can leverage communication context; however, fixed samplers allocate identical capacity to layer–relation neighborhoods with heterogeneous utility. Flat threshold-based controllers additionally exhibit state-dependent action semantics and reward signals confounded by concurrent encoder updates. We propose DHRL-MB, a message-budgeted graph-learning framework that decomposes sampling into two hierarchical control levels. A slow-timescale manager distributes a global integer budget across layer–relation coordinates, whereas a fast-timescale worker selects neighbor–edge instances within each assigned quota using a stochastic sampling-without-replacement policy. Controller rollouts are evaluated against budget-matched references while the graph encoder remains frozen, and encoder optimization begins only after both policies are fixed. This reward-isolated training schedule stabilizes action semantics and disentangles adaptive-sampling gains from representation learning. A relation-aware edge classifier subsequently propagates only the selected messages. Across four public NetFlow benchmarks, DHRL-MB improves macro-F1 over the strongest baseline by up to 3.42 percentage points under random splits and 6.67 percentage points under endpoint-disjoint evaluation, while retaining only 34% of full-neighborhood messages. These results demonstrate that hierarchical allocation improves balanced detection by concentrating limited computation on the most informative relations and graph depths.

title: Confidence-driven lightweight adaptive online deep learning for IoT intrusion detection
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm has become a technology used in homes, industry, agriculture, energy, and healthcare. Because of this technology’s widespread adoption and the weak security architecture of most IoT devices, the ecosystem has become an attractive target for cyberattacks. One mitigation technology for securing IoT networks is an intrusion detection system (IDS); however, most existing IDS cannot run on IoT edge hardware because they require substantial computational resources. Moreover, these IDS models are trained offline, making them difficult to adapt to data drift. To address these limitations, we proposed an online deep learning framework that combines an adaptive feature gate and a confidence-modulated learning rate. Experimental results on six IoT-based datasets show that the proposed framework outperformed online machine learning baselines on four datasets. The proposed model also outperforms three drift detection algorithms across all six datasets, achieving up to an 11.8 percentage-point improvement over reset-based drift methods. Post-training quantization reduces the model by up to 98% without degrading performance. The results show that the proposed framework reduces model size and adapts to data drift in real time without negatively impacting the model’s detection capability, making it ideal for edge deployment. However, minority-class detection remains a weak and important area to address going forward, as attack classes such as DNS spoofing in CIC-IoT, injection in NF-ToN-IoT, and malformed, SlowITe, and brute-force traffic in MQTTset exhibit high false-negative rates. The code used for our experimental validation is available in the GitHub repository, https://github.com/v-pragbe/Adaptive_Online_Deep_Quantization.git

title: Hybrid Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machine for Network Intrusion Detection Using NISQ‐Compatible Quantum Circuits
abstract: ABSTRACT The amount of cyber threats is growing at an exponential rate, and intelligent network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) that can cope with high dimensional and complex network data, is essential. Traditional machine‐learning (ML) approaches might not be as effective to identify complex hidden correlations between traffic attributes and at identifying advanced and unseen attacks. In this paper we suggest a classical–quantum hybrid kernel framework that enhances network intrusion detection. Using principal component analysis (PCA), network traffic features are normalized and dimensionality reduced to be compatible with noisy intermediate‐scale quantum (NISQ) devices, whilst preserving over 95% of the variance in the data. The classification is achieved by a fidelity‐based quantum kernel with a classical support vector machine(SVM). The proposed hybrid quantum kernel support vector machine (QK‐SVM)is tested using two datasets, CIC‐IDS2017 and CICIoT2023. Experimental results, achieving accuracy up to 98.1%, F1‐score up to 0.98, and anomaly detection rate of 97.6% with linear and RBF‐SVM baselines, are comparable to that of Random Forest. The results are based on the Qiskit Aer simulator and do not reflect the performance on actual quantum devices.

CyberPangolin-Net: A Chinese Pangolin Optimized Relation-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Forecasting and Identification of Cyber Hacking Breaches
abstract: The increasing complexity of cyber-attacks requires intelligent intrusion detection systems capable of accurately identifying malicious activities in cloud environments. This paper introduces a novel cybersecurity framework, CyberPangolin-Net, which integrates Chinese Pangolin Optimization (CPO), Relation-Aware Graph Learning, Graph Attention Networks (GANs), Capsule Learning, and Contextual Attention for cyberattack forecasting and intrusion detection. The proposed framework adaptively selects informative features, models complex attack relationships, and learns hierarchical intrusion patterns to enhance detection performance. The proposed method achieved 99.31% accuracy, 99.18% precision, 99.12% recall, 99.15% F1-score, and a macro-average AUC of 0.9974 on the NSL-KDD dataset. Furthermore, cross-dataset validation demonstrated strong generalization capability with accuracies of 98.74% and 98.21% on UNSW-NB15 and NF-UQ-NIDS-v2 datasets. The low inference latency of 2.06 ms per sample and lightweight architecture further demonstrate the suitability of CyberPangolin-Net for real-time cloud intrusion detection and secure cloud security applications.

Graph Wavelet Gated Recurrent Neural Network Based Attack Detection and Feistel Block Cipher Cryptography Model for Secure Communication in Vehicular Cloud Networks
abstract: Abstract Vehicular networks are widely regarded as a promising solution to enhance convenience and satisfaction in transportation. Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) play a crucial role in enhancing road safety, traffic efficiency, and secure communication among vehicles. With the growing adoption of VANETs and increasing service demands, optimizing resource utilization, ensuring low-latency data exchange, and addressing security threats remain key challenges in VANET. Thus, an advanced deep learning-based attack detection system combined with a routing protocol and an optimized encryption algorithm is developed for secure communication in Vehicular Cloud Networks. Initially, the vehicle nodes are deployed and clustered into nearby vehicles using Mobility Aware Adaptive Clustering Algorithm (MAACA). The Rhinopithecus Swarm Optimization Algorithm (RSOA) is employed to pick a cluster head by evaluating factors including transmission distance, vehicle degree, and link stability. After the clustering process, Directional Transmission-based Energy Aware Routing Protocol (DTEARP) is used to choose the best route for sending the data from the cluster head to the Road Side Unit (RSU). This approach reduces energy loss by avoiding unnecessary omnidirectional broadcasting and prolonging the network’s operational lifetime. Then during the data transmission, normal vehicles are identified from the attack vehicles using Graph Wavelet Gated Recurrent Neural Network (GWGRNN). Once the normal vehicle are identified, the information was securely stored in the cloud server using Feistel Block Cipher based Encryption (FBCE) algorithm. If it is an attack vehicle means then the alert message is given to the vehicle. Accuracy, NPV, and recall of the suggested approach are 96.08, 96.05, and 96%, respectively. The integration of a robust routing protocol with advanced attack detection enhances security in Vehicular Cloud Networks. This approach ensures reliable communication by preventing unauthorized access and mitigating potential threats.

title: Benchmark Accuracy Is Not Robustness: A Cross-Domain Study of ML-Based Intrusion Detection across IoT and Enterprise Traffic
abstract: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems often achieve strong performance on standard benchmarks, yet fail when deployed in a different environment. This paper investigates how well ML-based detectors transfer between IoT and enterprise traffic, using IoT-23 and UNSW-NB15 as two heterogeneous domains. Our experiments show that cross-domain performance drops sharply even after explicit feature alignment and limited target supervision, and that this drop is strongly asymmetric across transfer directions. Early detection experiments show that malicious signal is recoverable from partial traffic observations within a domain, but this property does not transfer equally between domains. The hybrid model that combines tabular, temporal, and prototype-based evidence provides interpretable insights into these failure modes, but does not consistently outperform simpler temporal baselines. Together our findings suggest that benchmark accuracy alone is a poor indicator of real-world robustness, and that intrusion detection system evaluation should place greater emphasis on cross-domain portability, data efficiency, and timeliness.

title: One Filter Is All You Need: Understanding Pattern Recognition in 1D Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON SYSTEMS AND CONTROL
abstract: Pattern recognition in sequential data is a fundamental problem encountered across digital communications, cryptography, and computational biology. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated strong performance in sequence classification tasks, the mechanisms by which they achieve this remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we examine how a simple one-dimensional CNN performs binary classification on sequences containing hidden target patterns, using artificially generated data under tightly controlled conditions that isolate network behavior from domain-specific noise. We demonstrate, through both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation, that a single convolutional filter aligned with the target pattern is sufficient for perfect classification. We further show that constraining the fully connected layer to have equal weights yields a substantial reduction in the number of parameters and extends accurate classification from sequences of 1,200 bits to 20,000 bits. The effects of sequence length and target pattern length on classification performance are also investigated. These results provide insight into the mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of shallow 1D-CNNs in sequence classification and suggest practical guidelines for the design of interpretable models.

title: Enhancing university network security through ML-based detection of DDoS and ARP spoofing attacks: a systematic review
abstract: Introduction University networks are increasingly vulnerable to Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) and Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) spoofing attacks due to open-access architectures, Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) practices, Internet of Things (IoT) integration, and dynamic traffic patterns. This study systematically reviews machine learning (ML)-based approaches for detecting these threats in university and related network environments. Methods Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, peer-reviewed studies published from January 2021 to January 2026 were identified through IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis Online, and Web of Science, with the final database search completed on 31 January 2026. Of 400 identified records, 200 studies met the predefined eligibility and quality criteria and were included in the synthesis. The review examined supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, deep learning, hybrid, and ensemble approaches with respect to detection performance, validation strategies, deployment readiness, computational efficiency, adaptability, and explainability. Results The findings indicate that many reviewed studies reported strong detection performance across supervised, unsupervised, deep learning, hybrid, and ensemble approaches. Hybrid and ensemble models frequently demonstrated strong reported results; however, these findings were not directly comparable across studies because of differences in datasets, attack scenarios, feature sets, validation procedures, and experimental environments. Benchmark datasets were used in 48% of the reviewed studies, whereas only 12% evaluated real university networks. Real-time detection was assessed in 40% of studies, while continuous learning, concept-drift detection, and model adaptation received comparatively limited attention. Discussion The evidence does not establish universal superiority of any particular learning paradigm and suggests that reported performance depends substantially on the evaluation context and methodological conditions. These findings highlight the need for adaptive, context-aware, cross-layer, and explainable intrusion detection approaches capable of addressing the operational characteristics of university networks.

A novel parallel multi-stage architecture for network intrusion detection
abstract: As cyber threats grow in frequency and sophistication, the need for accurate and efficient intrusion detection systems has become increasingly critical. This article proposes a novel parallel multi-stage network intrusion detection system designed to improve detection accuracy, reduce training and inference time and enhance the detection of attacks. In the first stage, our architecture features two modules running in parallel: a one-class support vector machine trained solely on benign traffic for anomaly detection, and a random forest classifier trained exclusively on malicious samples for attack classification. A lightweight rule-based component in the second stage integrates the outputs of both modules using pre-defined thresholds to issue the final verdict, distinguishing between benign traffic, known attacks and previously unseen attacks (zero-day). Evaluated on the intrusion detection evaluation datasets CIC-IDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 under a single protocol applied to both systems, the proposed approach improves balanced accuracy over the state-of-the-art at a lower inference cost, the latter driven principally by the size of the baseline's support-vector set. Ablation studies demonstrated that these thresholds, along with the rules, can be adjusted post-training to fine-tune the system's performance without requiring model retraining, offering operational flexibility.

title: An Adaptive Graph Neural Learning Framework for Real-Time Cyber Threat Detection in IoT and Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) made up of varying, distributed, and resource-constrained components and systems have brought with them new security issues. Many traditional IDS are less effective at detecting the rich relationships and temporal nature of today's network traffic, particularly. To address this, in this paper, the authors propose a new method for real-time Threat Detection in IoT and CPS using graph-based deep learning with the help of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). We formulate the network entities and interactions as a graph, and introduce the concepts of graph convolutions that allow us to model spatial and temporal relations. We give a whole architecture that includes data preprocessing, dynamic graph construction and classification based on graph neural networks (GNNs). To enhance the feature learning, the mathematic formulation is done through the message passing and attention weighted aggregation. Empirically, our model consistently outperforms traditional machine learning and deep learning techniques like SVM, Random Forest, CNN, and LSTM with accuracy of more than 98% and F1-Score of more than 0.97 compared to these models. Along with latency measurement on CPU and edge device, using three data subsets (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and EdgeIIoT) also ensures the effectiveness of the framework across data sources and deployability. It has demonstrated high detection capability of the different types of attacks and low false-positive rate and it can hence be used in real-time deployment in a resource-constrained IoT environment.

title: Reinforcement Learning-based Cybersecurity Model for Adaptive Intrusion Detection and Automated Responses
abstract: With growing cyber threats, we need adaptive intrusion detection with self-learning and automated action. This paper proposes a new Federated Soft Actor-Critic (FSAC) for real-time intrusion detection and response. Our re-view of reinforcement learning methods highlights key limitations in real-time scalability, robustness to adversarial attacks, and transparency. Our federated framework delivers 99.92% detection accuracy on CICIDS2018 with a 0.45% false positive rate, 2-3 times better than previous methods. Our approach combines the edge-fog-cloud model with attention-based aggregation for privacy-preserving, distributed threat detection. Our approach is benchmarked on five representative datasets (NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017/2018, AWID) and shows outstanding performance and scalability for production.

title: Protocol-Constrained Adversarial Evasion Against Transformer-Based Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) approaches that are transformer based demonstrate good performance in classification but are susceptible to protocol-oriented adversarial attacks. We present Appendix Protocol-Constrained Adversarial Evasion (PCAE), producing perturbations within protocol feasibility constraints to do so in a manner that does not corrupt the packets or leave us discovered. Our proposed model is an improving mechanism based on the threat model, the Conformal Prediction-Augmented Adaptive Defense (CPAAD), which is a multi-head self-attention encoder with distribution-free uncertainty quantification based on split conformal prediction. Assessed in enterprise (CICIDS2017 and CICIDS2018), IoT (N-BaIoT), and Industrial Control System /SCADA (SWaT) settings with FGSM, PGD and C&W attacks, CPAAD has a 90 or higher marginal coverage and a 61.4 level decrease in adversarial success compared to unprotected baselines and beats seven competing defenses by all metrics.

An AI-Driven Cybersecurity Framework for GSaaS: Threat Detection in Emerging Space Ecosystems
abstract: Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) is transforming satellite ground-segment operations through cloud-native, shared, and multi-tenant infrastructure, creating cybersecurity requirements that extend beyond conventional intrusion detection. This study proposes an AI-driven cybersecurity framework that integrates behavioural anomaly detection, supervised threat classification, contextual risk assessment, risk-aware edge–cloud processing, and policy-constrained response orchestration. A key contribution is the Analyst-Capacity-Aware False-Alarm Burden (AC-FAB) model, which extends conventional false-positive evaluation by relating generated false alarms to available analyst capacity and distinguishing detector-level false positives from those ultimately requiring human investigation. The framework is evaluated through complementary GSaaS-specific and benchmark experiments. A 100,000-event synthetic GSaaS dataset comprising 1,000 operational episodes is used to evaluate the integrated decision pipeline. Incorporating the autoencoder anomaly score into supervised classification reduces the false-positive rate from 7.61% to 6.98%, while risk-aware routing retains 80.09% of evaluated events for local edge processing. Policy validation across 20,000 generated response plans records no tenant-scope, session-scope, or action allow-list violations. Response orchestration reduces analyst-facing false positives from 1,272 to 530, corresponding to a 58.33% reduction in estimated false-alarm burden. Complementary evaluation on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15 demonstrates the effect of reconstruction-error threshold calibration, reducing false-positive rates from 38.68% to 3.61% and from 65.69% to 9.52%, respectively, relative to the 50th-percentile reference configuration. These findings show that GSaaS cybersecurity should be evaluated not only by detection performance, but also by operational risk, processing location, response-policy correctness, tenant isolation, and the human capacity required to investigate alerts.

TrustGuard-VehNet: An ensemble deep learning framework for trust modelling and malicious node detection in vehicular networks
abstract: Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) require reliable trust assessment and attack detection to protect safety-critical communication under rapid topology changes. This paper presents TrustGuard-VehNet, an ensemble deep-learning framework that combines a one-dimensional convolutional neural network for short-window behavioral features, a bidirectional long short-term memory network for temporal behavior, and graph attention for relation-dependent neighbor evidence. The fused representation supports continuous trust estimation, malicious-behavior classification, threshold-based isolation, and trust-aware next-hop selection. Within the evaluated controlled simulation, TrustGuard-VehNet achieved 97.8% trust accuracy, a 95.6% attack-detection rate, and 92.4% routing stability. Packet delivery ratio increased from 83.4% to 91.7%, while end-to-end delay decreased by 19.2%. The reported 18.9 ms value is simulation-side detection latency rather than execution time measured on an onboard vehicular processor. These results establish proof-of-concept performance for the reported configuration and motivate validation under broader mobility, channel, density, and hardware conditions.

A cross-domain review of artificial intelligence techniques for iot security, computer networks, image processing and smart agriculture in connected environments
abstract: The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven solutions across connected systems. However, these domains face persistent challenges such as heterogeneous datasets, limited labeled data, real-time processing constraints, privacy concerns, model interpretability, and poor generalization across environments. This review examines the application of major Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for solving classification, prediction, optimization, anomaly detection, routing, image analysis, and decision-support problems. The empirical patterns across the literature are summarized cautiously across studies. General lessons that emerged across the reviewed domains were also presented. Overall, the review provides researchers with a concise foundation for understanding current AI methods, their practical limitations, and future research directions in the aspect of connected environments. This article has tried to clarify various aspects and overall issues related to the use of AI techniques in computer networks, image processing and computer vision, smart agriculture and related intelligent systems. The authors believe that this is a comprehensive and integrated survey of these AI techniques in a number of application domains, with an emphasis on their practical suitability, their current empirical limitations, and future research directions. Thus, the article is informative to researchers in the field and may be a guide to future research on the development of robust, interpretable, scalable, and context-aware AI-based connected systems.
